events.text: Among the ash of the isle you took from {sov_isle} a single tea-house still stands, because nobody in your host thought it worth burning. Its keeper, Seol Harin, pours you a cup without being asked. Their partner held the isle's gate against you. They do not say so. They only pour.
events.arc: The Widow of the Raided Isle

choices.text: Drink it, and leave a domain-coin on the table

effects.log: You drink. The coin is still on the table a century later; nobody on the isle will touch it.

choices.text: Ask them what the gatekeeper's name was

effects.log: They tell you. You make yourself say it back. Seol Harin looks at you for a long time and then pours a second cup.

choices.text: Knock the cup from the table

effects.log: The cup breaks. Seol Harin sweeps it up without a word, and from that day the isle prays against you by name.

events.text: Seol Harin has crossed half of heaven to find you. {sov_hunter}, sworn by {sov_isle} to bring you down, is camped on the far side of your domain, and the widow has come to say they know the hunter's plan, and that they will tell it for a price.
events.arc: The Widow of the Raided Isle

choices.text: Pay their price: let the isle rebuild its gate

effects.log: The gate goes up again, and the plan you are told is true. The hunter walks into an empty valley.

choices.text: Read the plan from their mind instead

ok.log: You take it without asking. Seol Harin goes home knowing what you are.

fail.log: The mind closes like a fist. They leave, and the hunter learns you tried.

events.text: A god of a quiet domain sends you a mirror wrapped in grey silk and no letter. In the glass your face is calm. Behind it, very small, every domain you have taken burns at once, and in each fire someone is still trying to put it out.

choices.text: Keep the mirror by your seat

effects.log: You keep it where you can see it. Some nights you turn it to the wall.
The quiet god does not answer. Three of their neighbours close their borders that year.

events.text: Ryu Gaon, who counts your spoils, sets a new book before you: black covers, no title. "Every Calamity Star of the old ages kept a ledger," they say. "What it said on the last page is all heaven remembers of them. What shall I write on the first?"

choices.text: Write: conquest. Every domain, in order

effects.log: Ryu Gaon writes the word in a hand that does not shake. The book feels heavier at once.
The first page stays empty. Heaven guesses, and every guess is worse than the truth.

choices.text: Write a question: what is a star for?

effects.log: Ryu Gaon writes it and looks up at you, surprised. You do not answer, and they do not ask again.

events.text: A century on, one domain has been yours long enough to forget its old god. Its mortals below have stopped praying for rescue and started praying to you, timidly, the way a field prays to a storm. Mak Dohyeon, your marshal, asks what the host should do with it.

effects.log: The host learns to stand a watch instead of breaking one. The prayers below grow steadier.

choices.text: Strip it to the bedrock and move on

effects.log: The domain is left a bare cloud. The other gods count the days until it is their turn.

choices.text: Leave it alone and see what grows

effects.log: Nothing grows for fifty years. Then something does, and nobody can say what it is.

events.text: {sov_Isle} no longer sends one hunter. Oh Sanggil, an old tracker who once mapped the cloud-sea for the isles, has bound eleven of them into the League of the Long Count. Every raid you make, they write down. Every year you live, they add a name to their oath.

choices.text: Strike the League where it meets

effects.log: You find the hall and empty it. The League meets somewhere else the next year, with more names.

choices.text: Send Oh Sanggil a copy of your ledger

effects.log: The tracker reads every line of it. Their next letter is shorter, and it has your name spelt right.

choices.text: Fold yourself among the stars and wait

ok.log: The League hunts an empty sky for twenty years and starts to quarrel.

fail.log: Oh Sanggil finds the fold in the stars on the second night, and marks it on every map.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol, envoy of the Silent Hall, comes to bargain and does not sit. "The four pantheons will pay you a tithe of starlight every decade," they say, "if your host never crosses their borders again. Nobody has offered a Calamity Star this before. Nobody will again."

effects.log: The bargain is sealed in silence. Your host grows fat on starlight, and the borders of heaven grow quiet.
Yun Hwaseol bows as if you had agreed, and walks home through a heaven that has just been told no.

choices.text: Name a price nobody could pay

effects.log: You ask for a god's true name. Yun Hwaseol writes it down without a word and goes away.

events.text: Forty years of tithes, and your host has forgotten how to march. Mak Dohyeon finds the captains playing go on the battlements with pieces of the starlight they were paid in. "Is this what we are now?" the marshal asks you. "Tax-collectors of the sky?"

effects.log: Mak Dohyeon salutes and says nothing. The board on the battlements stays set for a hundred years.
You lead the host past every border at a walk and harm nothing. Heaven does not sleep that night.

events.text: The four pantheons answer your refusal together. Their gate-wardens close every road of heaven to your host at once: no festival will seat you, no market will sell to you, and at each border a warden of the Throne of Storms stands in the rain, waiting.

choices.text: Break one gate to open them all

ok.log: The gate of the Storms falls, and the other three open quietly before you reach them.

fail.log: The warden holds. You go home wet and wounded, and the roads stay shut for a decade.

effects.log: You make a heaven of your own domains. It is smaller. It is yours.

events.text: Someone paid your price. A minor god of a small river below has given up their true name to buy peace for their neighbours. They stand in your hall with no name now, smiling a little, waiting to see if a Calamity Star keeps a bargain.

choices.text: Keep it. Your host never crosses again

effects.log: You keep it. The nameless god goes home, and their river is the only quiet water in heaven.
You speak it once, softly, and hand it back. The god weeps, and the other gods stop understanding you.

events.text: Ha Yeonu was a child on the isle you took from {sov_isle}. You brought them home because they bit your hand. Now they are a god in their own right, and they stand at your left as your host gathers, and the captains have begun to call them the Little Star.

effects.log: The captains cheer. Ha Yeonu does not. They only look at the ledger, and you see they mean to read every page.

choices.text: A star has no heir. Tell them so

effects.log: Ha Yeonu bows. That night they walk out of your sky to find a path of their own.

choices.text: Send them home to their isle

effects.log: Ha Yeonu goes back to the ash they came from and starts to rebuild it. They write to you every year.

events.text: A second Calamity Star has risen. Dokgo Seon, a god of a lesser domain, raids in your style and under your colours, and the gods of heaven can no longer tell whose host has come to their gate. Dokgo Seon sends you a gift: a cup cut from a god's throne.

choices.text: Crush them. There is one star

effects.log: You go out and end the Second Star's host in a single night. The cup stays on your table.

choices.text: Drink from the cup. Two stars, then

effects.log: You drink, and the sky has two calamities in it. Heaven does not sleep for a century.

choices.text: Ignore them. Let them learn what it costs

effects.log: Dokgo Seon learns it slowly, and alone, and you watch.

events.text: The Book of Fates of the Heavenly Court opens of its own accord on a page that has your name at the top and nothing under it. A summons follows, sealed in white wax: the Court will write the rest of the page, with you in the room or without.

choices.text: Go to the Court and stand there

effects.log: You climb the Court's stair alone, your host left at the bottom. The judges did not think you would come.

choices.text: Burn the summons on your stair

effects.log: The wax smells of lilies as it burns. Somewhere in the Court, a warrant is written in red.

choices.text: Read the empty page before they write it

ok.log: For a moment you see what the page would say. You will not tell anyone.

fail.log: The page stays empty for you, and only for you.

events.text: The Court of Heaven hears you for nine days. Every god you raided sends a witness; every isle sends a list. On the ninth day the chief judge asks only one thing: "If we let you go, what will you do?"

effects.log: They sentence you to a thousand years of standing still. You agree, and the whole Court goes quiet.

choices.text: Read them the first page of your ledger

effects.log: You read it aloud. The judges write nothing down, and send you home unsentenced, and afraid.

events.text: The Court's warrant-bearers come for the god who burned a summons: twelve of them, each carrying a lantern that does not flicker. They do not fight. They simply stand at the borders of your sky, and wherever their light falls, your domains are no longer yours.

choices.text: Put out the lanterns one by one

ok.log: Twelve nights, twelve lanterns. The bearers go home in the dark.

fail.log: Three lanterns go out. Nine remain, and three of your domains stay lit and lost.

choices.text: Let them stand there for a century

effects.log: They stand. You let them. In the end the lanterns burn down, and heaven wonders who won.

events.text: Ryu Gaon is old now, and the ledger is nearly full. Markets of heaven you have not raided in a thousand years still shutter when your shadow crosses them. "Your terror has outlived your raids," Ryu Gaon says. "It goes on without you. Is that what you wanted?"

choices.text: It is exactly what I wanted

effects.log: Ryu Gaon writes that down too, and closes the book for the night.

choices.text: Ask them how to make it stop

effects.log: Ryu Gaon thinks for a long time. "Walk through a market and buy something," they say.

choices.text: Let them rest. Take the pen yourself

effects.log: Ryu Gaon gives you the pen and sleeps for a whole season. Your hand is worse than theirs.

events.text: Ha Yeonu stands where you stood, at the edge of your sky, with your host behind them. They have read every page of the ledger. "I will keep half of it," your heir says. "The other half I will undo, one domain at a time. You may watch."

effects.log: You step back from the edge. The Little Star begins, and the gods of heaven do not know what to fear.

choices.text: Hand them the pen and the book

effects.log: The ledger changes hands. Ryu Gaon, very old, smiles for the first time in a thousand years.

events.text: The thousand years of your sentence end on an ordinary morning. You have stood still the whole time, and the stars that dimmed for you have come back one by one. The judges come to see if you are still a calamity. You do not know the answer yourself.

choices.text: Step off the spot, and raid nothing

effects.log: You walk to the nearest market and buy a pear. The whole market holds its breath and then, slowly, lets it go.

choices.text: Step off it and give the word

effects.log: Your host has waited a thousand years. Heaven learns the sentence taught you patience, and nothing else.

events.text: The last page of the ledger. Ryu Gaon writes the final domain on it and lays the pen down. Every name in heaven you could take is in the book, in order, as you said on the first day. There is nothing left to conquer, and your host is still waiting for a word.

effects.log: You close it. The host waits for a word that does not come, and slowly learns to live without it.

choices.text: Turn the book over and begin again

effects.log: There is a back cover. Ryu Gaon starts writing on it.

events.text: The ledger is full, and the first page is still the one you left: nothing, or a question. Ryu Gaon hands you the book and asks to go home. "I have written down everything you did," they say. "I never once wrote down why. That page is yours."

effects.log: You write a single line. Ryu Gaon reads it, nods, and leaves your service in peace.
The page stays empty. In the end it is the page heaven remembers best.

events.text: The captain who held the gate of {sov_god} against you does not flee when the domain falls. Mak Dohyeon kneels in the ash with their spear across their knees and asks to serve whoever is strong enough to have beaten them. "I am not loyal," they say. "I am useful."

effects.log: Mak Dohyeon rises and takes command of your host within the hour. Nobody objects twice.

choices.text: Make them a captain, and watch

effects.log: They take the lesser post without a word, and serve it better than anyone above them.
Mak Dohyeon goes. A god without a domain gets one loyal captain back, and nothing else.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon has rebuilt your host in their own image: smaller, quieter, never seen until it is too late. The old captains hate it. "They want banners and drums," the marshal says. "Banners are for gods who need to be seen. Do you?"

effects.log: Your raids become rumours. The gods of heaven fear the silence more than they ever feared the drums.
The drums come back. Heaven hears you coming for three days before every raid, and shakes for all three.

events.text: A letter from {sov_god} reaches Mak Dohyeon, not you. Ryu Gaon reads it first, as they read everything: the fallen god offers the marshal their old post back, and a pardon, if they open one door of your sky on one night.

choices.text: Give the letter to Mak Dohyeon, unopened

effects.log: The marshal reads it in front of you and burns it. "I said I was useful," they say.

choices.text: Burn it before they see it

effects.log: Mak Dohyeon never knows. You do, every time you look at them.

choices.text: Let them have it, and watch which door

ok.log: No door opens. The marshal burns the letter and never mentions it.

fail.log: A door opens a crack, and closes. You never learn who opened it.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon has served you two hundred years. Today they ask for one raid of their own choosing: the domain of {sov_god}, who once sent them out to die at a gate. "Not for you," the marshal says. "For me. Once."

choices.text: Give them the host for a night

effects.log: Mak Dohyeon comes back at dawn without a spoil and without a word. You never ask what they did.

choices.text: Refuse. The host has one will

effects.log: The marshal salutes. It is the stiffest salute you have ever seen.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon's hands have begun to shake. A god's hands do not shake, they tell you, and then hold one up so you can see that theirs do. "I have one campaign left in me," the marshal says. "Choose it well."
events.arc: The Marshal Sets Down the Spear

choices.text: Choose the hardest domain in heaven

effects.log: Mak Dohyeon grins for the first time in centuries and begins to plan.

choices.text: Choose none. Let them rest now

effects.log: The marshal sets the spear in your hall and does not pick it up again.

events.text: The last campaign of Mak Dohyeon. It takes a year to reach the gate and an hour to break it. At the top of the stair the marshal sits down, quite suddenly, and asks you to finish the rest yourself.
events.arc: The Marshal Sets Down the Spear

effects.log: You finish it. Mak Dohyeon watches every stroke, and nods at the last one.

choices.text: Leave the gate standing, and carry them home

effects.log: You carry your marshal home. The god of that domain never learns why they were spared.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon has taken up gardening, badly. The captains bring them seeds from every domain you raid, and the garden on the edge of your sky is a riot of plants that should not grow together. "They argue," the old marshal says, pleased. "Like an army."
events.arc: The Marshal Sets Down the Spear

effects.log: You plant a single seed from your oldest domain. It comes up black and gold and very stubborn.

choices.text: Ask them to train your new marshal

effects.log: They agree, and are as hard on the new marshal as they were on the gate of {sov_god}.

events.text: Ryu Gaon has run out of ink. The ledger takes only one kind, they explain: ground from the seals of the domains it records. "It is a very old book," they say. "It wants to be paid in what it writes."

effects.log: The ink comes out the colour of a domain at dusk. The ledger writes more easily after.

choices.text: Make them write in plain ink

effects.log: The plain ink fades in a year. Ryu Gaon writes every page again from memory.

events.text: The ledger has started writing on its own. In the night Ryu Gaon hears the pen move, and in the morning there is a new line: a domain you have not raided yet, and a date.

choices.text: Read the date, and arrive early

ok.log: You arrive a year early. The domain falls without knowing why.

fail.log: The date shifts as you read it, and you arrive a year late to an empty hall.

effects.log: The ink will not cross out. Ryu Gaon tears the page instead, and the book is quiet for a while.

events.text: Ryu Gaon asks to stop writing in the black book and keep a second one, small and green, of the things you did not destroy. It is very thin. They read it to you on the night of the new year anyway.

effects.log: It takes less than an hour. You ask them to read it again.

choices.text: Add a line to it yourself

effects.log: You leave one temple standing that you meant to burn, only so the green book has a new line.

events.text: A copy of your ledger is being sold in the markets of the Green Assembly: every raid you made, in order, with the hour and the number of the host. Ryu Gaon is white with anger. "Only two people have read the book," they say. "One of them is you."

choices.text: Believe Ryu Gaon, and look elsewhere

effects.log: You look elsewhere. Ryu Gaon sees you do it, and serves you harder than ever.
You have them watched. They know, and say nothing, and the ledger's hand grows smaller.

events.text: The copyist is found: a young god of the Green Assembly with a perfect memory, who stood in your hall as a servant for one year and read the ledger over Ryu Gaon's shoulder. They sold it to the League of the Long Count. They are not sorry.

choices.text: Take their memory of the book

effects.log: The young god forgets a year of their life. The League keeps the copy they already have.

choices.text: Hire them to keep the green book

effects.log: They keep it beautifully. It is still very thin.

choices.text: Let them go. The truth is the truth

effects.log: Heaven reads your ledger openly now. Some gods are more afraid. A few, strangely, are less.

events.text: The League of the Long Count has used the copied ledger well. Every raid since has met a wall already built, a vault already moved. Oh Sanggil sends you a note: "You raid like a book. Books can be read."

ok.log: You break every habit in the book at once. The next wall is in the wrong place.

fail.log: Old habits run deeper than you thought. The vault is gone before you arrive.

effects.log: Oh Sanggil keeps your note. You hear it is pinned above their maps.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon reads the roll of your host aloud, as they do on the first day of each century. It takes all day. At the end they read the names of the ones who did not come back from the last century's raids. That takes until midnight.

effects.log: You stand until midnight. The host sees you do it, and some of them weep.
You leave at dusk. Nobody remarks on it, and everyone notices.

events.text: The vault of your spoils has grown so large that Ryu Gaon keeps a map of it. In the farthest room sit the things nobody can use: a god's cradle, a festival mask, a box of letters in a language older than the pantheons.

effects.log: They are love letters, between two gods who no longer exist. You read them all in one night.

choices.text: Send the cradle back to its god

effects.log: It is returned without a note. The god sends nothing back, and their borders close an hour later.

events.text: You walk through a market of heaven on foot, alone, plainly dressed. Every stall is shut by the time you reach it. One old seller of paper lanterns did not see you coming in time, and stands frozen over the last lantern, waiting.

effects.log: You pay twice its price. The seller does not dare refuse, and hangs your coin on a string for luck.
Behind you, one by one, the stalls open again. You hear them through the whole length of the street.

events.text: A god of a southern domain, newly risen, comes to court you, which nobody has done in an age. They talk for an hour. You say nothing kind, because nothing kind will come. At the end they bow and say, "I see. It is not you. It is the path."

effects.log: They go home and tell everyone the Calamity Star thanked them. Nobody believes it.

choices.text: Let them think it is you

effects.log: They go home and tell nobody. It is easier for both of you.

events.text: Your host has made up a song about you. It is not flattering. It is mostly about how often you are right, and how terrible that is to watch. They sing it under their breath on the march, and stop when you turn your head.

choices.text: Ask them to sing it out loud

effects.log: They sing it, very badly, all the way to the gate of the next domain.
Your verse is worse than any of theirs. The host loves you a little for it, in a frightened way.

events.text: Ryu Gaon counts the stars nearest your sky that have dimmed in your time. It is a long count. One of them, far out, has begun to shine again on its own, and nobody can tell you why.

effects.log: It shines a little brighter every century. You never ask it why.
It goes out without a sound. The count is whole again, and colder.

events.text: A letter is left on your stair, pinned under a white pebble. It is from Baek Yuhwa, the young sword of the first wave. "I am to come again," it says. "They have not told me when. I wanted you to know I am not afraid any more. That is not true. I wanted you to know."

effects.log: You write three lines and leave them under the same pebble. In the morning the pebble is gone.
The letter stays on your stair all winter. Nobody in your host dares to move it.

events.text: A second letter, under a grey pebble now. Baek Yuhwa has been made to train with the Guardians of the gates, and is better than they were, and asks you a question no assassin should: "When you were young, who taught you to stand your ground?"

effects.log: You write the name of your first teacher, the only one. Baek Yuhwa's answer is a single word: thank you.

choices.text: Tell them the ground taught you

effects.log: The next letter says only: that is a very lonely answer.

events.text: The letters have stopped. In their place a sword in a white sheath has been left on your stair, Baek Yuhwa's own. A note is tied to the hilt: "They are watching my letters. If I do not have it, they cannot make me use it on you. Keep it until I come."

choices.text: Keep it in your hall, unsheathed

effects.log: It hangs above your seat. Your host thinks it is a trophy. You let them think so.

choices.text: Send it back with an escort

effects.log: The sword goes back to the Guardians in the night. Baek Yuhwa is not punished, and does not write again.

events.text: The white sword above your seat has begun to hum, softly, at the hour when the stars change watch. Its owner is near. Somewhere in heaven, a wave is gathering, and the sword knows which side of the line its owner will stand on.

choices.text: Listen to it and learn the wave's road

ok.log: The hum rises and falls like a march. You learn the road and leave it empty.

fail.log: The hum is only grief. You learn nothing from it but that.

choices.text: Wrap it in cloth so it can sleep

effects.log: It sleeps. You do not, for a week.

events.text: Heaven has no more waves to send, and Baek Yuhwa has no more orders. They come to your gate alone, in grey now, not white, and ask the question they have carried since the first night: "Why did you spare me? Every time. Why?"

choices.text: Because you held your place, shaking

effects.log: Baek Yuhwa is quiet for a long time. "So did the others," they say at last.
"Then I will stay until you do," Baek Yuhwa says, and sits down on your stair.

choices.text: Tell them to go before you change your mind

effects.log: Baek Yuhwa goes. On the road they turn once, and you are still watching.

events.text: Baek Yuhwa has stayed on your stair for twenty years. They have not drawn a sword in that time. They sweep the steps, and argue with Ryu Gaon about the ledger, and once a year they practise the form they were taught to end you with, slowly, so you can watch.

effects.log: You do the form together, slowly. Neither of you finishes the last stroke.

choices.text: Ask them to teach your host to defend

effects.log: Baek Yuhwa teaches your host the Guardians' art of standing still. Your raids grow strange and patient.

events.text: The Righteous Immortals who sent Baek Yuhwa against you have named them a traitor. A Guardian's warrant has come to take them back to the gates, where traitors are made into gateposts and stand for an age. Baek Yuhwa does not run. They wait to see what you will do.

choices.text: Meet the warrant at your border

ok.log: The warrant goes home without its prisoner. Heaven files it away and does not send another.

fail.log: You hold the border, but the warrant's bearer sees you wounded, and heaven learns it.

choices.text: Speak for them before the Guardians

effects.log: You go to the gates of heaven in person, unarmed. The Guardians have never seen that, and tear up the warrant.

events.text: Baek Yuhwa has founded something: not a sect, not a host, a small house at the edge of your sky where gods who were once sent to kill someone come to learn to stop. There are nine of them now. One was sent against you in a wave you do not remember.

choices.text: Visit the house, and sit with them

effects.log: You sit with them for an evening. Nobody talks about why they are there.

choices.text: Send them starlight from your vault

effects.log: They buy a second room with it. Baek Yuhwa sends back a single grey pebble.

events.text: Baek Yuhwa is very old, for a sword. They ask you to come to the edge of your sky at the hour when the stars change watch, as on the first night. "I want to see it once from your side," they say. "Just once. Then I will know."

choices.text: Stand beside them and look out

effects.log: You stand together and look out at heaven. Baek Yuhwa laughs, very softly, and says: oh.

choices.text: Give them your place, and stand where they stood

effects.log: You stand where the first wave stood. It is smaller from there than you remembered.

events.text: A young sword in white comes to your border carrying a second sword wrapped in grey: Baek Yuhwa's, who did not come home from the last wave. The young one is Ok Hana, Baek Yuhwa's student. "My teacher said to bring it to you," they say. "Not why. Only to bring it."
events.arc: Ok Hana and the White Sheath

effects.log: You take it. Ok Hana watches your hands and seems to find something in them.
"Then I will keep it against you," Ok Hana says, very politely, and goes.

events.text: The grey-wrapped sword in your hall has a name cut into the hilt that is not Baek Yuhwa's. Ryu Gaon looks it up in the old rolls: it was the name of the first god you ever raided, centuries before Baek Yuhwa was born. Their teacher's teacher's sword, then.
events.arc: Ok Hana and the White Sheath

effects.log: Ok Hana comes back to read the hilt for themselves, and stays an hour, and leaves without anger.
You keep it. The sword hums sometimes, at the hour when the stars change watch.

events.text: Ok Hana has kept the sword against you for thirty years and become very good with it. They come at last, not in a wave, alone and openly, at noon, and draw the sword at the edge of your sky. "I do not want to end you," they say. "I want you to see this."
events.arc: Ok Hana and the White Sheath

choices.text: Meet the form with your own

ok.log: The duel lasts until dusk, and neither of you is hurt. Ok Hana bows and sheathes the sword.

fail.log: Ok Hana's last stroke stops a finger from your throat. They sheathe it and leave you to think.

choices.text: Do not draw. Watch the form

effects.log: You watch it all. It is Baek Yuhwa's form, finished at last.

events.text: Ok Hana has opened a hall in the Upper Realm's isles to teach the white form. They write to you, which no Righteous Immortal has ever done: "I tell them about you. Not the raids. The night you watched the form, and did not draw."
events.arc: Ok Hana and the White Sheath

effects.log: You write. Ok Hana pins the letter above their door, and the students argue about it for a century.

choices.text: Send nothing, and stay away from the isles

effects.log: You stay away. It is the kindest thing you can do, and you know it.

events.text: Cheonbeol's hood was all that was left at the end of the last wave. It lies in your hall, empty, still keeping its shape around a face that was never there. At night it turns, very slowly, to face whoever is awake.

effects.log: It hangs above your gate. No god of heaven has knocked on it since.

choices.text: Keep it in a box, unseen

effects.log: The box sits in your vault. Some nights you hear it turn inside.
It will not burn. The fire lies down around it like a dog.

events.text: The Executioner's blade has been found in the cloud-sea, far below your sky, where it fell. It has ended one god in every age. This age, it ended none. The gods who found it bring it to you on a cushion, at a distance, not touching it.

ok.log: The blade is lighter than it should be, and it does not want you. It stays anyway.

fail.log: The blade will not lift for you. It lies on the cushion and waits for a hand that is not yours.

effects.log: They drop it back into the cloud-sea. Somewhere in heaven, a new age begins to wait for it.

events.text: A new Executioner has been chosen, as one is chosen in every age. They are young, and have no face yet, and they have come to your gate to ask for the old hood. "It is not a threat," they say. "I cannot begin without it."

effects.log: They put it on. It fits. They bow, and go, and the next age of heaven begins.

choices.text: Keep it. Let heaven go without

effects.log: Heaven goes without an Executioner. It is the first age in memory without one.

events.text: The box in your vault has gone silent. When you open it, the hood is gone, and in its place is a single folded strip of white cloth. Written on it, in a hand nobody has ever seen: "Not this age."

effects.log: You keep it close. You never learn whether it is a pardon or a promise.

choices.text: Read it aloud to your host

effects.log: Your host is very quiet for a month. Then the drums start again, louder.

events.text: A figure in a hood stands at the far edge of your sky and does nothing. Ryu Gaon says it has stood there for a month. Mak Dohyeon says it is not their business to fight what does not fight. Nobody says the name, but the whole host knows it.

choices.text: Go out and stand opposite it

effects.log: You stand opposite the hood for a day and a night. It does not move. Neither do you.
The hood is gone a year later. Nobody saw it leave.

events.text: The hood is back, and closer. It has been watching your waves. When Guardian Cheolbyeok fell at your border, the hood was there, and when the twins of the Silent Hall came to your bed, it was there too. It is learning how you fight.

choices.text: Fight a wave badly, on purpose

ok.log: You fight the next wave in a style that is not yours. The hood leans in, puzzled.

fail.log: The hood is not fooled. It goes away satisfied.

choices.text: Fight it as you always fight

effects.log: Let it learn, you think. Let it learn what it is coming to.

events.text: A white strip of cloth is left on your stair in the night. On it, in a hand nobody has ever seen: "I am the last. Not yet." The host takes it as a threat. Ryu Gaon, who has read every warrant heaven ever sent, says it is something rarer: a courtesy.

choices.text: Leave a strip of your own at the edge

effects.log: You write: I will be here. In the morning it is gone.
The watch doubles. Nothing comes, for a long time, and that is worse.

events.text: Ha-eun and Ha-ram, the twins of the Silent Hall, are at the foot of your bed again one morning, as they were in their wave. This time they carry no knives, only a jar of something dark. "Sleep," Ha-eun says. "You have not, in a century. We can tell."
events.arc: The Twins of the Silent Hall

effects.log: You sleep for a year. When you wake the twins are still there, and your host is still yours.
They go without argument, leaving the jar. You do not touch it for a long time.

events.text: The twins come back every few decades to see how you sleep. Ha-ram says you dream of every domain at once. Ha-eun says you dream of nothing, and that it is worse. They argue about it on your stair until dawn, like the old friends of someone else.
events.arc: The Twins of the Silent Hall

effects.log: You tell them. They stop arguing, and stay a week longer than usual.

choices.text: Ask them to dream for you

effects.log: They take a dream from you each and carry it away. You sleep easier, and remember less.

events.text: Ha-eun has died, as gods of the Silent Hall sometimes do, by going quietly into sleep and not coming back. Ha-ram comes alone and sits at the foot of your bed and says nothing at all. After an hour you realise they want you to keep watch while they sleep.
events.arc: The Twins of the Silent Hall

effects.log: You keep watch all night over one of the gods heaven sent to end you. Nothing comes.

choices.text: Give them the jar of dark sleep

effects.log: Ha-ram sleeps, and wakes, and thanks you, and goes home.

events.text: The stair that Wonhyo-seon climbed on their knees still has the marks of them, worn into the stone, one on every step. Your host avoids them. A young captain says that if you step in one, a star goes out.

choices.text: Step in one, in front of the host

effects.log: Nothing happens. The host does not believe you, and still walks around them.
The new stone is smooth by evening. By morning the marks are back.

events.text: Pilgrims have started coming to the stair. Mortal-born immortals of the isles, mostly, who climb it on their knees in Wonhyo-seon's marks and chant. Your host does not know whether to stop them. They are praying against you, after all.

effects.log: They climb, and pray, and go home. The stars do not go out. They only flicker, politely.
The stair is closed. The pilgrims chant at the bottom of it instead, which is louder.

events.text: An old monk climbs the stair on their knees and reaches the top on a clear morning. It is Wonhyo-seon, much older, who was not ended by you after all. "I came back to finish the climb," they say. "Not the fight. The climb."

choices.text: Offer them a seat at the top

effects.log: They sit, and look out, and chant one last verse, and leave the way they came.

choices.text: Climb down beside them on your knees

effects.log: You climb down beside the monk on your knees. Your host watches from the walls in total silence.

events.text: Lady Seomun's army left its war-banners in the field when it broke: the banners of every sect you emptied, a hundred of them. They are folded in your vault. The isles have asked, through three envoys, to have them back.

effects.log: The banners go home. The isles do not thank you, but they hang them again, and they stop sending envoys.
A hundred banners of the emptied sects fly over your sky. The isles weep to see them.

events.text: Lady Seomun comes in person, very old now, to ask for one banner only: the one their own teacher carried. They will not kneel. "I lost to you," they say. "I have not lost to anyone else, before or since. That is not the same as owing you."

effects.log: They take it in both hands and walk out without another word.

choices.text: Ask them what they would trade for it

ok.log: They trade you the true account of the battle, which no isle has ever written down.

fail.log: They laugh at you and leave, and the banner stays on your wall.

events.text: The returned banners hang again on the isles. Under every one, the immortals have added a strip of black cloth with your name on it. Ryu Gaon says it is a mourning-band. Oh Sanggil, of the League, says it is a promise.

effects.log: You accept it. The League grows by three isles that year.
You accept that too. Grief lasts longer than oaths, in the end.

events.text: Guardian Cheolbyeok's armour was forged from the Southern Gate itself, and the gate has stood half-built ever since. The Guardians of heaven cannot finish it without the armour, and the armour is in your hall.

effects.log: The Southern Gate is whole again within a year. The Guardians salute your sky every dawn, very stiffly.
It does not fit. It is too heavy, and too honest. You take it off and hang it up.

events.text: A Guardian of the Southern Gate brings you news: Cheolbyeok was not ended in their wave. They have been standing in the half-built gate all this time, as a gatepost, holding it up with their own shoulders. They have asked to see you once more.

effects.log: Cheolbyeok cannot move their head. They look at you sideways and say, "You are smaller than I thought."
The armour goes, and Cheolbyeok steps out of the gate at last, and sits down for the first time in centuries.

events.text: Cheolbyeok, free of the gate, has taken up a post at your own border: not against you, they insist, only beside you. "A gate is a gate," the old Guardian says. "Somebody has to know who is coming in."

effects.log: They stand there for an age. Nobody comes in that you did not want.

choices.text: Ask them to guard your host instead

effects.log: They guard your host on every raid, and refuse to strike a single blow.

events.text: The wound from the last wave you fought has healed into a pale line that catches the light at the hour when the stars change watch. Your physician, a god of the Green Assembly who is paid twice their worth to come, says it will never fade.

effects.log: It is the only mark on you heaven has managed to leave. You wear it openly.

choices.text: Have it hidden with an array

effects.log: The array holds. Underneath, the line still catches the light, and only you can see it.

events.text: A rumour runs through your host: the next wave is already gathering, and it will be the worst of all. Nobody knows who started it. The captains want orders. The cooks want to know whether to make more rice.

effects.log: The host eats well for a month. The wave, if it is coming, comes to a host that is not hungry.
It was the wind. You never find anyone else.

events.text: The first decade with no wave coming. Your host does not know what to do with it. Captains sharpen blades that will not be needed. Mak Dohyeon has set them to building a wall around nothing, to keep their hands busy.

effects.log: It is a very good wall. It keeps nothing in and nothing out, and the host is proud of it.

choices.text: Send them on a raid instead

effects.log: They go gratefully. Heaven, which had begun to breathe, stops again.

events.text: Ryu Gaon has written the names of all six waves at the front of the ledger, above the domains: every Righteous Immortal and Guardian heaven sent, in the order they came. It is the only page of the book that is about someone else.

effects.log: You read them all. It takes a long time. Your host listens without a sound.

choices.text: Add your own name under them

effects.log: Ryu Gaon hesitates and then writes it. It looks very small among the others.

events.text: A white feather drifts down into your hall from a sky that has no birds. Ryu Gaon says the Righteous Immortals send one to every god they have given up on. Mak Dohyeon says it is only a feather.

effects.log: You keep it on the table by the ledger. It never yellows.

choices.text: Send it back on the wind

effects.log: The wind takes it. A year later a second one comes down, a little grey.

events.text: A sword is found driven into the cloud at your gate with no one near it, its hilt wrapped in a Righteous Immortal's white cord. Mak Dohyeon will not let anyone pull it out until you have seen it. It is a challenge, or a grave.

ok.log: It comes out clean. On the blade, written small: I could not come. Forgive me.

fail.log: It will not move. It is still there a century later, and the host walks around it.

effects.log: The host leaves offerings at it, in the end. You never ask whose.

events.text: The healer who sews your wounds after a wave is a god of a quiet domain who never asks how you got them. Tonight they do. "I heal them on both sides," they tell you, "the gods you send home and the ones who come for you. I wanted you to know."

effects.log: They nod and finish the stitch. You both know it is the strangest thanks you have ever given.

choices.text: Pay them double to heal only you

effects.log: They take the starlight and keep healing both sides, and you let them.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has made camp just outside your sky, close enough that the smoke of their fire drifts across your border at dusk. They do not hide it. {sov_Isle} has sworn them to bring you down, and they want you to know they are patient.

choices.text: Send a captain to put out the fire

effects.log: The captain comes back with the fire's ash in a jar and a message: next time, come yourself.

choices.text: Walk out and sit at their fire

effects.log: You sit across the fire from {sov_hunter}. Neither of you speaks. It is the longest night of the year.
The smoke drifts across your sky every dusk for ten years. Your host learns to sleep through it.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has learned your hours. They strike once, at the hour you always walk the wall, and their arrow takes the stone beside your hand. It was not a miss. It is a sentence: I know where you will be.

choices.text: Walk the wall at the same hour tomorrow

ok.log: No arrow comes. {sov_hunter} has learned something about you that is worth more than a shot.

fail.log: The second arrow grazes you. You walk the wall anyway, and the host sees it.

effects.log: You become a god of no habits. It is tiring. It is also safe.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has been wounded by someone else: a god of the Throne of Storms who did not want a hunter in their weather. They lie in the rain at your border, alone, and their isle is too far away to come for them.

choices.text: Bring them in and heal them

effects.log: You heal the hunter sworn to end you. They thank you, very stiffly, and leave the moment they can walk.
Their isle comes for them, slowly. They live, and remember who did not help.
The rain stops. Heaven hears of it, and the hunters of every isle swear again.

events.text: {sov_hunter} comes to your gate unarmed, years after you healed them. "My oath is not broken," they say. "It is only paused. I want you to know the day I take it up again, so it is a fair hunt. I will send you a feather."

effects.log: You agree. Every spring you look for a feather, and every spring there is none.

choices.text: Tell them never to take it up

effects.log: "That is not yours to tell," they say, and smile for the first time, and go.

events.text: A map is delivered to your hall by a frightened crane: your own sky, drawn better than your captains could draw it, every gate and stair and hidden vault. In the corner a small seal: Oh Sanggil, tracker of the isles. Under it: "So you know I know."

choices.text: Send back a map of the League's isles

effects.log: Ryu Gaon draws it, beautifully. Oh Sanggil writes back: three mistakes. Good.

choices.text: Move every vault in a night

effects.log: Your host moves every vault by dawn. The next map arrives a month later, with the new places.

choices.text: Hang the map in your hall

effects.log: It is a better map than yours. You start using it.

events.text: Oh Sanggil comes in person to the edge of your sky, under a white flag nobody asked them to carry. They are small and very old and carry a measuring-rope. "I want to walk your border," they say. "Only walk it. For the map."

effects.log: They walk your border for a month and you walk beside them. You learn more about your sky than in a thousand years.
They nod and walk the other side of the border instead, measuring it from outside.

events.text: The League of the Long Count has a new oath, Oh Sanggil writes. Not to end you, which they have failed to do for a long time, but to map everything you take before you take it, so that when the Star is gone, the isles can be rebuilt as they were.

effects.log: You leave a list on your stair every decade: what you mean to take. The League copies it and says nothing.

choices.text: Raid what they have not mapped yet

ok.log: You beat them to an isle. Oh Sanggil sends you a single word: well.

fail.log: Their map is already done. They were a step ahead, as always.

events.text: Oh Sanggil's last map arrives with their seal broken: they have died, peacefully, on an isle you never raided. It is a map of the whole of heaven as it was before you. In the margin, in a shaking hand: "For whoever comes after the Star. Even if it is the Star."

choices.text: Keep it in the ledger, at the back

effects.log: It is the only thing in the ledger you did not cause.
The League hangs it in their hall. They name a new tracker. The new one is not as good.

events.text: The League of the Long Count calls its last hunt: every hunter of every isle you have raided, a thousand of them, all at once, led by Oh Sanggil from a litter because they can no longer walk. They do not come in secret. They send you the date.
events.arc: The Last Hunt of the League

effects.log: You set out your host on the open cloud on the day they named.

choices.text: Go alone to Oh Sanggil's litter

effects.log: You walk out alone, past a thousand drawn bows, to the old tracker's litter.

events.text: The two lines face each other across the cloud: your host and a thousand hunters of the isles. Oh Sanggil raises a hand from the litter. Nobody moves. The old tracker is waiting to see which of you is more tired.
events.arc: The Last Hunt of the League

choices.text: Break the line before the hand falls

ok.log: The League breaks and scatters. It will not gather again in your time.

fail.log: The line holds, and you are wounded in the middle of it. The hunters carry Oh Sanggil home slowly.

effects.log: You lower it. The League goes home, unbroken and unbeaten, and calls it a victory.

events.text: Oh Sanggil is too weak to sit up. You kneel by the litter, past a thousand bows. "I hunted you for six hundred years," they say. "I never once wanted to catch you. I only wanted somebody to be counting."
events.arc: The Last Hunt of the League

effects.log: Oh Sanggil laughs, and the League lowers its bows, and goes home.

choices.text: Tell them the count is over

effects.log: "It is never over," the tracker says, and gives you their rope.

events.text: The League of the Long Count has disbanded. Its last act was to send you its book: every raid you ever made, counted by the isles, in a thousand hands. It is longer than Ryu Gaon's ledger. It has things in it Ryu Gaon never knew.
events.arc: The Last Hunt of the League

effects.log: It takes a year. At the end you know what you were, as heaven saw it.
It sits by the ledger, sealed. Two books about the same god, and you will read only one.

events.text: You raided {sov_isle}: the very power you served in the Upper Realm, before you were a god. Among the ash your host finds the room you slept in as a young immortal, kept exactly as you left it, a cup still on the sill. Someone has been dusting it for an age.

effects.log: You close the door on it and post a guard. Your host does not understand, and does not ask.
You take it. It is a very ordinary cup. You drink from nothing else for a century.

choices.text: Burn the room with the rest

effects.log: It burns like any room. You watch it to the end, so nobody can say you did not.

events.text: The one who dusted your room for an age comes to find you: an old elder of {sov_isle}, who taught you the first form you ever learned. They are not angry. They want to know one thing: "Was it us? Did we make you into this?"

effects.log: The old elder nods, as if they had always known, and goes home to teach differently.

choices.text: Tell them no. It was the path

effects.log: "Then I am sorry for the path," they say, "and not for you." It hurts more than yes.

choices.text: Tell them you do not know

effects.log: You sit together a long time with that, and then they pour you tea in the cup you took.

events.text: {sov_Isle} has made a law that your name may not be spoken on its isles. Children there are taught it anyway, in whispers, the way children are always taught the names of things they must not say. Some of them have begun to come to your border to look.

effects.log: They run. One of them stops and looks back, and does not run again.

choices.text: Close the border to the young

effects.log: The children stop coming. The whispers do not.

events.text: The old elder who taught you has died. {sov_Isle} does not send word: a single cup arrives on your stair, the pair of the one you took, unwrapped. Ryu Gaon says it is the custom of the isles to send a cup to the last student. They did not know you were still counted.

choices.text: Go to the isle for the rites

effects.log: You stand at the back. Nobody turns around, and nobody asks you to leave.

choices.text: Set both cups on your table

effects.log: The two cups stand together on your table for the rest of your life.

events.text: On the isle you took from {sov_isle}, someone has built a school among the ruins: a roof of broken arrays, desks of fallen gate-stones. The teacher is a young immortal who lost everything in your raid. They teach the children to read using your war-banners.

effects.log: A crate of books arrives with no seal. The children read every one, and the teacher burns the crate.
The school grows slowly. Your banners are worn thin with reading.
The children cry, and learn to read on stones instead.

events.text: The school in the ash has its first graduates: twelve young immortals who can read, count and form arrays, and who know exactly who burned their isle. The teacher asks, through a crane, whether you will come to see them graduate.

effects.log: You stand at the back. One graduate recognises you, and bows, and you do not know what it means.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay away

effects.log: You send a jade brush for each. Eleven are kept. One is sent back, broken.

events.text: One of the graduates of the school in the ash has become the finest array-master of the isles, and has built a ward around {sov_isle} that you cannot break. They send you the plans of it, openly. "So you will not waste your host trying," the note says.

ok.log: You find the one flaw in it. You leave it alone, and write them where it is.

fail.log: The ward holds. It is the first thing in a thousand years you cannot take.

effects.log: {sov_Isle} sleeps safe for the first time since you came. You are, to your surprise, glad.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has an apprentice, Jang Mirae, who has been sent alone to scout your sky. They are caught by your host within an hour, very embarrassed, sitting in a tree of your garden with a notebook full of wrong measurements.
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Lost the Trail

effects.log: You correct their measurements and send them home with a good map. {sov_hunter} is not pleased.
They go home empty-handed and are scolded. They come back, alone, the next year.

events.text: Jang Mirae comes back every few years now, always caught, always in a different tree. {sov_hunter} no longer sends them. They come on their own, and admit it. "I do not want to hunt you," they say. "I want to know what you are."
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Lost the Trail

effects.log: You tell them more than you have told anyone. They write it all down, and their hand shakes.

choices.text: Tell them to choose a side

effects.log: "I have," they say. "Theirs. That is why I need to know."

events.text: Jang Mirae is a hunter of the isles in their own right now, and the best one. They have never once tried to strike you, and their notebook on the Calamity Star is studied in every hall of the League. They send you a copy.
events.arc: The Apprentice Who Lost the Trail

effects.log: It is fair. It is the fairest thing anyone has written about you. You do not enjoy it.
You correct three things. Jang Mirae prints the corrections, with your name.

events.text: {sov_Isle} is rebuilding, slowly, on the cloud where you left it. They have chosen not to rebuild the great gate. Instead, where it stood, they have put up a long low wall with nothing written on it, and every immortal who passes lays a hand on it.

choices.text: Lay your hand on it too, at night

effects.log: The stone is warm from a thousand hands. Yours is the only cold one.
You watch them build for a year and never come closer.

events.text: Someone saw your handprint on the wall, or says they did: a cold mark among the warm ones that will not wash off. {sov_Isle} is divided. Half want to cut the stone out. Half want to leave it, so that the wall remembers everyone who was there.

effects.log: They leave it. Children dare each other to touch the cold mark.
You smooth it out. The isle wakes to a wall with one place that is too smooth.

events.text: The rebuilt {sov_isle} holds a festival for the first time since your raid. It is small and slightly sad and full of lanterns, and the elders have sent you, of all gods, an invitation, written on the back of one of their old war-banners.

choices.text: Go, and stand at the edge

effects.log: You stand at the edge with a lantern nobody gave you. Nobody asks you to leave.

choices.text: Send a lantern and stay home

effects.log: Your lantern is the largest at the festival. Nobody knows where it came from. Everybody knows.

events.text: The gate you let Seol Harin's isle rebuild is finished: smaller than before, with a tea-house built into one of its towers. Seol Harin sends you a cup from it, wrapped in grey silk. "The gate is for the hunters," the note says. "The tea is for whoever comes."

effects.log: You drink at the gate. The hunters of the isle watch you from the walls and do nothing.
It sits on your table. Mak Dohyeon thinks it is poison. Ryu Gaon thinks it is worse: kindness.

events.text: Seol Harin has grown old keeping the tea-house in the gate. They have trained an heir to the cups, a nervous young immortal, and they want you to meet them. "So they know what you look like," Seol Harin says, "and so they are not afraid of the wrong thing."

effects.log: The young one pours for you with shaking hands and does not spill a drop. Seol Harin is very proud.

choices.text: Tell them to fear the right thing

effects.log: "What is the right thing?" the heir asks. You find you cannot tell them.

events.text: Seol Harin has died in the tea-house at the gate, at the table where they poured for you. They have left you nothing but a name, in a letter: the name of the gatekeeper you asked for once, long ago, and that they made you say back.

choices.text: Say the name once more, alone

effects.log: You say it to the empty sky. It is the last time anyone in heaven will say it.

choices.text: Have it cut into your own gate

effects.log: Your gate carries the name of a gatekeeper you defeated. Nobody understands why.

events.text: Your host finds a trap at the edge of your sky: not a net or a ward, but a single flower of the isles planted in the cloud, which only blooms when the Calamity Star passes. When it blooms, every hunter of {sov_isle} will know.

effects.log: It comes up easily. Three more are found the next week, further in.
It blooms whenever you pass, very beautifully. The hunters come, and find only the flower.

events.text: The isles have posted a bounty on you in every market of heaven. The price is not in starlight: it is a seat on the council of {sov_isle} for whoever brings you down. Ryu Gaon reads it out. "That is a good price," they say. "For them."

effects.log: You double the bounty in your own name. The markets of heaven are very confused.
Nobody collects. A few try, and go home early.

events.text: A bell from {sov_isle}'s great hall hangs in your vault, taken in the raid. It rings by itself on the isle's feast days, far from home, calling a hall that is no longer there.

effects.log: It rings in its own hall again. The isle does not thank you, but they ring it every feast.
It rings into cloth now, softly, on the feast days. You always hear it anyway.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has been seen sleeping in a market of heaven, worn out, with their bow across their knees. A merchant who fears you sends word to your hall. It would be very easy.

effects.log: They wake and never learn how close you came. The merchant does.
They wake under a blanket woven with your colours. The whole market laughs, and they never forgive it.

events.text: The elders of {sov_isle} send you a formal letter, very long and very polite, setting out every crime of your raid in order, and asking at the end for nothing. Ryu Gaon says it is not a demand. It is a record. They want you to know it exists.

choices.text: Have it bound into the ledger

effects.log: The two accounts sit side by side. They do not always agree.

choices.text: Send back a list of your own

effects.log: You list what you did not take. It is short. The elders read it twice.

events.text: Among the spoils of {sov_isle} are the robes of the rank you held there, long ago, before you were a god. They are still folded the way the isle folds them. Your host does not know what they are.

effects.log: They still fit. That is the worst thing about them.

choices.text: Give them to a young immortal of the isle

effects.log: A young immortal of {sov_isle} wears your old rank. They will never know whose it was.

events.text: Ryu Gaon has counted the oaths the isles have sworn against you: four hundred and eleven, in four hundred and eleven halls. "None of them has been kept," they say. "None of them has been broken either. They are all still waiting."

choices.text: Ask them to count again next century

effects.log: The count grows by forty-two. Ryu Gaon does not look surprised.
It was a small hall on a small isle, and the oath was sworn by a child. You remember the raid.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol, envoy of the Silent Hall, comes to your hall for the first time and does not sit, though you offer a seat three times. "The Hall wishes to know your price," they say. "Not for peace. Nobody expects peace. Only for a decade's warning before you come."

effects.log: You name a domain's worth of starlight. Yun Hwaseol writes it down and does not blink.

choices.text: Tell them warnings are for friends

effects.log: "Then we are agreed," says Yun Hwaseol. "We are not friends." They bow and go.

choices.text: Ask them why they will not sit

effects.log: "Because if I sit, I will stay too long," they say, which is the only joke they ever make.

events.text: The Silent Hall has paid. Every decade a sealed letter comes, and in it a warning-bell you are to ring before you march on any domain of the Hall. Mak Dohyeon hates it. "A raid with a bell is a visit," the marshal says.

effects.log: You ring the bell before every raid on the Hall. They are always ready, and you win anyway.

choices.text: Ring it once, and then stop

effects.log: The Hall learns what a broken bargain sounds like: silence. Their envoy does not come again for a century.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol comes back after a long absence, older, and this time they sit. "The Hall has nothing left to bargain with," they say. "I came to ask for myself. My sister's domain is next on your list. I know it is. Is there anything I can give?"

choices.text: Take their sister's domain off the list

effects.log: Yun Hwaseol says nothing for a long while. Then they stand up, and bow lower than any envoy should.

choices.text: Ask what they think it is worth

ok.log: They tell you a secret of the Silent Hall in exchange. It is worth the domain.

fail.log: They cannot find a price, and leave, and the list stays as it is.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol has been dismissed by the Silent Hall for bargaining too well with a Calamity Star. They come to your gate with one box of belongings. "I have nowhere else that would understand," they say, and wait for you to laugh.

choices.text: Give them a room, and a seat

effects.log: They take the seat. They stay too long, as they said they would, and become your envoy instead.

choices.text: Send them to Baek Yuhwa's house of stopping

effects.log: They go. You hear they are good at it.

events.text: Envoys of all four pantheons come on the same day, which has not happened since the founding of heaven. The Will of Heaven, the Silent Hall, the Green Assembly and the Throne of Storms each make an offer, and each offer is that you raid one of the other three.
events.arc: The Offer of the Four Halls

choices.text: Take the Will of Heaven's offer

effects.log: You march on a domain of the Silent Hall with the Will of Heaven's blessing. Heaven watches it split.

choices.text: Take the Throne of Storms' offer

effects.log: You march on a domain of the Green Assembly. The Storms rumble with satisfaction.

choices.text: Send all four envoys home with nothing

effects.log: Four envoys walk home on the same road, not speaking to each other.

events.text: The pantheon that bought your raid has grown proud. Its gods walk the markets of heaven as if they owned them, and the pantheon you struck for them has sworn vengeance. The envoy who paid you sends a second purse, much larger.
events.arc: The Offer of the Four Halls

effects.log: Two pantheons are wounded and one grows fat. Heaven calls you a weapon, and you do not like it.

choices.text: Raid the one that paid you instead

effects.log: You march the other way. Every pantheon learns that a Calamity Star cannot be bought twice.

events.text: Four envoys came; one went home with a bargain, and that bargain ended badly. Now the envoys of all four pantheons agree on one thing for the first time: no pantheon will ever again buy a raid from a Calamity Star. They sign it in your sight.
events.arc: The Offer of the Four Halls

effects.log: Your name sits under theirs. It is the only treaty of heaven with a Calamity Star's name on it.
They sign it anyway. It holds, which surprises everyone.

events.text: A god you threw down has not left your sky. Seo Dowon held a small domain of orchards before you took it, and now they tend the trees of your garden for nothing, every morning, as if nothing had changed. Your gardeners are afraid to tell them to stop.
events.arc: The Gardener Who Was a God

effects.log: Seo Dowon bows to you every morning and goes on pruning. The garden has never been so good.
Seo Dowon goes without a word. The trees drop their fruit early that year.

events.text: Seo Dowon has grafted a cutting from their old orchard onto your oldest tree. "So the domain is still somewhere," they say, "even if it is yours." The tree flowers twice a year now, once in your colours and once in theirs.
events.arc: The Gardener Who Was a God

effects.log: Your host comes to sit under the tree on both feast days. It is the only place in your sky they laugh.
The graft comes away clean. Seo Dowon watches, and says nothing, and goes on pruning.

events.text: Seo Dowon's old worshippers below have found out where their god is. They send small offerings up through the clouds: a plum, a ribbon, a child's drawing of a tree. They arrive in your garden, addressed to a gardener.
events.arc: The Gardener Who Was a God

effects.log: Seo Dowon keeps every one in a box under the grafted tree. Faith rises a little in your sky, too.

choices.text: Give Seo Dowon their domain back

effects.log: You hand back the orchards. Seo Dowon weeps, and then goes on pruning your garden anyway, out of habit.

events.text: Seo Dowon is fading, as a god without a domain fades. They ask to be buried under the grafted tree, which is not a thing gods ask. "I want to be a gardener at the end," they say. "It is the only thing I was ever good at."
events.arc: The Gardener Who Was a God

effects.log: You bury them under the tree with your own hands. It flowers three times that year.

choices.text: Return them to their old orchard

effects.log: You carry them home. Their worshippers below dream of a gardener that night.

events.text: The domain of War is yours, and Mujin of the Thousand Banners is not. Their banners still hang in the war-hall, a thousand of them, each the colours of a battle Mujin won. They stir whenever you walk under them, as if waiting to be called.

effects.log: The banners rise and turn toward you. Every army below feels it at once.
It takes a month. The war-hall is very bare, and very quiet.

events.text: Mortal generals below have begun to pray to War again, and the prayers that reach you are not for victory. They are for it to end quickly. Mujin always answered the first kind. Nobody has ever answered the second.

effects.log: Wars end faster below. Generals call it a curse. Their soldiers call it something else.

choices.text: Answer the first kind, as Mujin did

effects.log: Victories below grow great and loud. The prayers grow louder too.

events.text: Mujin of the Thousand Banners comes to the edge of the domain, without a single banner, and asks to see the war-hall once. They have not come to fight. "A god of war without war," they say, "is only someone who remembers being angry."

effects.log: Mujin walks the hall end to end and touches one banner, the first. Then they go.

ok.log: You win. Mujin bows, and seems relieved to have been beaten fairly once more.

fail.log: Mujin wins, and takes nothing. "I wanted to know if I still could," they say.

events.text: The domain of the Sky came with a coil of silver rope that Cheonho, Who Hangs the Stars, used to hang them. Every night one star comes loose somewhere, and someone has to climb up and tie it. Cheonho did it every night for an age.

choices.text: Climb up and tie it yourself

effects.log: You tie your first star. It hangs a little crooked, and the mortals below love it.
Stars fall all over the sky below. The mortals make wishes. Heaven makes complaints.

events.text: You have tied a hundred stars now, and your knots are getting better. The mortals below have named one of the crooked ones after you, in a language heaven does not speak. Ryu Gaon finds out what it means: the one that came to stay.

effects.log: It stays crooked. It is the brightest in that quarter of the sky.
It hangs straight. The mortals below do not notice, and you are, strangely, disappointed.

events.text: Cheonho, Who Hangs the Stars, is found sitting on a cloud below the domain, watching the sky with their hands in their lap. They have not tied a star in all the years since you came. "Your knots are bad," they say. "They hold. That is all a knot must do."

effects.log: Cheonho teaches you the old knot, very slowly. Their hands remember better than they do.

choices.text: Give them the rope back for one night

effects.log: Cheonho ties every loose star in heaven before dawn, weeping, and gives you the rope.

events.text: The domain of Fire has one hearth at its heart, the First Hearth, which Hwarin tended since the first flame. It must be fed every day with something that matters to the one who feeds it. Hwarin fed it songs. Today it is your turn.

choices.text: Feed it a raid you regret

effects.log: The flame takes it and burns blue for a day. You feel lighter, and worse.
The hearth roars. Every fire in heaven flares at once.
It sulks and burns low. The forges below go cold for a month.

events.text: Hwarin of the First Hearth sends a message: the hearth is unhappy, and the hearths of every mortal home below are guttering with it. "It wants what it used to have," they write. "It wants to be fed by someone who loves it."

choices.text: Let Hwarin feed it once a year

effects.log: Hwarin comes on the longest night and sings to it. The mortal hearths burn warm all winter.

ok.log: It takes a century. Then the hearth begins, a little, to sing back.

fail.log: It will not take your love. It only takes what you are.

events.text: The First Hearth has kept something of everything you fed it. When you lean close, you can hear the raid you regretted, still burning, or the terror, still roaring. Ryu Gaon asks if they may write down what the fire says.

effects.log: Ryu Gaon fills a whole new book. It is the truest account of you yet.

choices.text: Bank the fire for a century

effects.log: The hearth sleeps under its ashes. The domain is warm, and silent.

events.text: The domain of Death has a river, and on the river a ferry that Baekun the Pale Ferryman poled for an age. The ferry is still running. Nobody is poling it. The souls of mortals below are crossing on their own, and some of them are landing on the wrong bank.

choices.text: Pole it yourself for a night

effects.log: You pole it till dawn. The souls are very polite to the Calamity Star, and very frightened.

choices.text: Let the souls find their own way

effects.log: Most do. The ones who do not wander the domain asking for directions.

events.text: One of the souls you ferried was from an isle you raided, long ago, before they fell below and were born mortal. They recognise you on the ferry. They say nothing for the whole crossing, and on the far bank they say, "Thank you for the ride."

effects.log: They nod, and walk on into the dark. You pole the ferry back alone.
They walk on. You pole back. It is the right silence, or the wrong one.

events.text: Baekun the Pale Ferryman stands on the far bank of their own river and asks to be taken across. They have never been a passenger. "I want to see where they all go," they say. "I never had time."

effects.log: You pole Baekun across their own river. They step off and do not look back.
Baekun takes it and stands in the boat for a long moment. Then they push off, home.

events.text: The domain of Fate came with a loom. On it, unfinished, is the cloth Unmyeong the Weaver was weaving when you took the domain: the fates of a thousand mortals below, and in one corner a single thread of your own colour, very short.

effects.log: Your thread grows a hand's breadth. Somewhere below, a thousand fates shift a little.

choices.text: Leave the loom as Unmyeong left it

effects.log: The cloth hangs unfinished. The mortals below live lives nobody is weaving.

events.text: The mortals whose fates you shifted with your thread are dreaming of you below: not of a Calamity Star, but of a stranger who helped them once on a road. None of them has met you. All of them have.

effects.log: You walk into a dream below and help a mortal with a cart. They thank you. You wake changed.
The dreams stop. The fates go back. Your own thread is as short as it was.

events.text: Unmyeong the Weaver sends you a skein of grey thread with no note. Ryu Gaon, who knows the old signs of the Silent Hall, says it is the colour used to finish a cloth. "They are asking you to finish it," Ryu Gaon says. "Or to let them."

effects.log: The Weaver comes for a night and finishes the cloth. Your corner is still short. It is woven tight.

ok.log: You finish it. It is not beautiful. It is done.

fail.log: The grey thread knots in your hands. Unmyeong comes the next night to untangle it.

events.text: The domain of Dreams has a bed at its centre where Mongsa the Sleeper slept and dreamed the dreams of every mortal below. Since you took it, nobody sleeps in it, and the mortals have begun to dream only of you.

effects.log: You sleep, and dream a thousand mortal dreams at once. You wake knowing every name below.
Mortal children wake crying every night. Their parents pray for the old god.

events.text: Sleeping in the Sleeper's bed has changed your dreams. You dream now of the domains you took, from the side of the ones who lost them: the gate falling inward, the stair you climbed seen from below. You wake every morning more tired than you were.

effects.log: You learn heaven from below, a night at a time. It does not make you kinder. It makes you slower.
The dreams stop. The mortals below dream of you again, and wake crying.

events.text: Mongsa the Sleeper has been awake since you took their domain, and a god who dreamed for an age cannot bear being awake. They come to your hall with red eyes and ask for one night in their own bed.

effects.log: Mongsa sleeps, and the mortals below dream of fields for the first time in a century.
You hand Mongsa back the Dreams. They are asleep before you finish speaking.

events.text: The crown of {sov_god}, who held {sov_domain} before you, sits in your vault. It is not a crown of gold: it is a circle of their worshippers' names, written on a band of light. New names are still appearing on it.

effects.log: The names press against your head like a crowd. You take it off after an hour.
{sov_god} keeps it in their small exile. They read a new name off it every morning.

events.text: Every pantheon keeps a seat for each god of heaven at its great feast, even for those it will never seat. Yours is at the far end of every table, and a servant still lays a cup there. The Will of Heaven's servant has asked whether to stop.

choices.text: Tell them to keep laying it

effects.log: The cup stays at the far end of the table. It is never filled. It is never taken away.
The cup is gone the next feast. You notice, every feast, after that.

events.text: The worshippers below {sov_domain} still bring their offerings, though the god they knew is gone. A grain of rice, a ribbon, a small clay horse. Your stewards ask whether to keep the offerings or send them on to {sov_god}.

effects.log: {sov_god} receives a sack of small offerings with no note. They know where it came from.
The offerings pile up in your vault. Faith in your sky rises, a little, unwillingly.

events.text: The gods you have thrown down have formed a council of their own in a grey corner of heaven. They meet once a century, without domains, and talk. Their first motion is a polite letter to you, asking you to stop making new members.

choices.text: Reply that you will consider it

effects.log: They frame your reply. It is the first thing they have won in a long time.
{sov_god} arrives at the grey council the same week. They are made chair.

events.text: A god of the Green Assembly you have never raided climbs your stair to offer you their domain freely, before you can take it. "I would rather give it," they say, "than have my worshippers watch it taken."

effects.log: They go home with their domain, shaken, and their worshippers below light a thousand candles.
It is the easiest domain you have ever taken. It is not the same as taking one.

events.text: The Silent Hall has, for the first time in its history, made a sound: a single bell, rung once, when your host crossed its border. Ryu Gaon says the Hall has decided you are worth breaking its silence for. Mak Dohyeon says it was a warning.

effects.log: The Hall goes silent again, for good. You are not sure what you said.
The Hall does not ring again. It does not need to.

events.text: The domain of Life is a garden without walls, and Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, left every seed in it planted when you took it. Nothing has grown since. The seeds are waiting, Ryu Gaon says, for a god who is not a calamity.

effects.log: You plant a single seed with your own hand. It sits in the earth for a decade, deciding.
The seeds wait. Below, fewer children are born that century.

events.text: The seed you planted has come up: a thorny little shrub with black leaves and one white flower. Gods of the Green Assembly come at night to look at it over the wall. None of them has ever seen anything grow from a Calamity Star's hand.

effects.log: They come every night. One of them leaves a watering-can.

choices.text: Pull it up before it seeds

effects.log: It comes up in your hand, thorns and all. You are not sure why you did it.

events.text: Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, comes to the wall of the garden at last. They are very old and smell of rain. "Something grew," they say. "I did not think anything would. May I plant the rest?"

effects.log: Saengmo plants all day. Below, it is the best spring in a thousand years.
You plant every seed with Saengmo watching. Half of them grow thorns.

events.text: The domain of Beasts is restless. Horang, Lord of the Wild, left it without a word, and the great beasts of heaven have gathered at its edges to see who the new lord is. A white tiger the size of a hall sits outside your gate and stares at you.
events.arc: The Lord of the Wild Waits

effects.log: You stare until dusk. The tiger yawns, and lies down across your gate, and stays.

ok.log: It goes, and the beasts of heaven know who holds the Wild.

fail.log: It does not go. It only blinks, very slowly.

events.text: The white tiger has had cubs on your stair. Your host will not go near them. Mak Dohyeon says beasts of heaven only den with a lord they trust, and that this is a very bad sign for a Calamity Star's reputation.
events.arc: The Lord of the Wild Waits

effects.log: The cubs grow up chasing your captains through the halls. Your host grows, despite itself, gentler.

choices.text: Move them out to the wild

effects.log: The tiger carries them away one at a time and does not come back.

events.text: Horang, Lord of the Wild, comes back to their domain at last, on foot, scarred, and very thin. They do not ask for it back. They ask only to walk among the beasts once. Every beast in the domain is already turning toward them.
events.arc: The Lord of the Wild Waits

effects.log: Horang walks all night, and the beasts follow. In the morning they are gone, both lord and beasts.
You hand Horang back the Wild. The white tiger looks at you once over their shoulder.

events.text: The domain of the Harvest is a single golden field that feeds the harvests below. Pungnyeon of the Golden Field walked it every day of their reign, and now it is yours, and the wheat is leaning toward the gate as if waiting for someone.

effects.log: You walk it every day for a season. The harvests below are good.

choices.text: Have the host walk it for you

effects.log: The host walks it in step, like a march. The harvests below ripen in rows.

events.text: The mortals below have learned that a Calamity Star walks their harvest field. In their harvest songs you have become a stern old reaper who walks the rows and takes one sheaf in ten. You have never taken a sheaf.

effects.log: You take your tithe. The songs are pleased to be right.

choices.text: Take nothing, and let the songs be wrong

effects.log: The songs stay. The harvests stay good. Some songs are kinder than the truth.

events.text: Pungnyeon of the Golden Field sends you a single sheaf of wheat at harvest, tied with a grass knot. Ryu Gaon says it is the old sign between neighbours: the field is well, and so is the one who walks it.

effects.log: You tie yours with a knot you invent. Pungnyeon writes to ask how it is done.
The sheaf dries on the ledger's cover. It is the only gentle thing on it.
