events.text: The domain of the Sea pulls at you. Haeryong, Keeper of Tides, held the tides with their breath, and since you took the domain, the seas below have been holding their breath too. Fishing boats sit on flat water. Nothing moves.

effects.log: You breathe out, slowly. Below, the tide comes in for the first time in a year.

choices.text: Let the sea learn on its own

effects.log: It learns, badly. Storms come out of nowhere, and the fishers below curse your name.

events.text: Breathing for the sea has slowed your own breath. You breathe now with the tides below, in and out twice a day, and when you lose your temper the seas below rise. Ryu Gaon has started to time your moods by the harbours.

effects.log: The harbours below have the calmest century in their history. Your host thinks you are ill.

choices.text: Let your temper be the weather

effects.log: The seas rage with you. Sailors below call you the Black Tide.

events.text: Haeryong, Keeper of Tides, rises out of the cloud-sea at the edge of your domain, vast and grey and slow. "The sea has your breath now," they say. "It will not take mine back. I came to see what it learned from you."

effects.log: Haeryong watches the slow tides below for a day, and sinks back into the cloud, satisfied.

ok.log: The sea below rises in a single wave and falls. Haeryong bows to it.

fail.log: The storm breaks loose and goes where it likes. Haeryong has to calm it.

events.text: The domain of Thunder came with nine drums, each as big as a hall, and no drummer. Noegong of the Nine Drums beat the weather of the world below on them. Since you came, the skies below have been silent, and the rains have not come.

effects.log: Your thunder is not Noegong's: it is irregular and very loud. The rains come, sideways.

choices.text: Let the host beat them in step

effects.log: The rain falls below in perfect marching time. It is very strange to watch.

events.text: The rains below have learned your drumming. They come when you are angry and stop when you are thinking. A farmer below has built a small shrine to the Drummer Who Thinks Too Much, and leaves you rice wine in a cracked bowl.

effects.log: The rains are better. The shrine below gets a second bowl.
The farmer below keeps the shrine, and keeps complaining to it, which is a kind of faith.

events.text: Noegong of the Nine Drums comes to listen. They sit on a cloud below your domain for a whole season with their eyes shut while you drum. At the end they open them. "Badly," they say. "But it is weather. Keep it."

effects.log: Noegong teaches you the slow roll of the first drum. The storms below grow musical.
Noegong takes the ninth drum and goes. Their thunder and yours answer each other every spring.

events.text: The domain of the Mountains has one peak at its heart, and on it a hollow in the rock where Daeak of the Unmoving Peak sat for an age without moving. The mountains below have begun to shift since you took it. Small landslides. A pass closing.

effects.log: You sit, and do not move, for a year. The mountains below settle.
The mountains below walk a little each century. The maps of mortals are all wrong.

events.text: You have learned to sit still, which no Calamity Star has ever done. Your host comes to the peak to ask for orders and finds you unmoving. Mak Dohyeon waits a month and then gives the orders themselves.

effects.log: Your host raids under Mak Dohyeon's orders for a year while you sit. It is a gentler year.
The mountains below shiver as you stand. Your host cheers.

events.text: Daeak of the Unmoving Peak comes to the foot of their mountain and stays there, unmoving, for ten years, until you come down to see why. "Waiting," they say. "It is the only thing I know how to do. I am very good at it."

effects.log: You wait together for a year. Neither of you says what you are waiting for.
Daeak climbs it in a single day, the fastest anyone has ever seen them move.

events.text: The immortals of your raided isles have found a way into {sov_world}, your Pocket World. They are not there to fight. They have come to hide among its people, in the one place in heaven where the Calamity Star does not raid.
events.arc: The Refugees of the Pocket World

effects.log: They build houses in {sov_world} and keep their heads down. Your world grows a little crowded.
They go back to the ruins of their isles. {sov_world} is quieter and smaller.

choices.text: Let them stay, and watch them

effects.log: They stay, and your eye stays on them. They feel it every night.

events.text: The refugees in {sov_world} have married into its people, taught its children their arrays, and built a hall that looks very much like the hall of the isle you burned. The people of {sov_world} love them. Some have begun to fear you.
events.arc: The Refugees of the Pocket World

effects.log: You walk in. Everyone stands. A child of {sov_world} asks you, in an isle accent, what you want.
It burns. {sov_world} learns that its god is the Calamity Star, too.

events.text: The hunters of {sov_isle} have learned where the refugees went. They ask your leave, by letter, to enter {sov_world} and bring their own people home. It is the first time a hunter of the isles has ever asked you for anything.
events.arc: The Refugees of the Pocket World

effects.log: The hunters walk {sov_world} unarmed. Some refugees go home. Most stay.
Your Pocket World is closed to the isles. The refugees stay, and so does their grief.

events.text: A child of {sov_world} with an isle grandparent has become a young cultivator of real talent, and has asked to go up to {sov_isle} to study. They need your leave to pass out of your world. They are not afraid of you. That is new.
events.arc: The Refugees of the Pocket World

effects.log: They go up to the isle you raided and are welcomed there, as a grandchild.
They stay, and study alone, and are better than anyone on the isle anyway.

events.text: The people of {sov_world} have begun to dream of you, and the dreams are not kind: a star that falls on their roofs at night. Their temples are full, but the prayers are all the same: please do not look at us.

choices.text: Stop looking at them for a century

effects.log: You turn your eye from {sov_world}. Its people sleep easily for the first time.
You walk among them in daylight. They are polite. They are still afraid.

events.text: A century without your eye on them, and {sov_world} has grown in ways you did not plan: its own festivals, its own small heroes, a new temple to a god they made up themselves. The made-up god looks a lot like you, but kind.

effects.log: You let them. It is the best thing about you, and it is not you.
You come back. The made-up god's temple is empty by spring.

events.text: An old priest of {sov_world} comes up to your hall, which nobody from there has ever dared. "We are not afraid of you any more," they say, shaking. "I came to tell you so. I am afraid of you. But the children are not. I thought you should know."

effects.log: The old priest goes home and tells the children the Star said thank you. Nobody believes it.

choices.text: Ask why the children are not

effects.log: "Because you have never come," the priest says. "They think you are a story."

events.text: Below, mortals have begun to build temples to you, not out of love: they pray that the Calamity Star pass them by. Their high priest, Cha Soyul, a mortal who has never seen a god, sends you their first prayer written on a black tile: "Not us."

effects.log: You pass the temple's city by. Below, it is called a miracle, and the temples double.
The temples go on praying. Fear, it turns out, does not need an answer.

choices.text: Send Cha Soyul a dream of yourself

effects.log: Cha Soyul wakes having seen you, and is very quiet for a year, and then builds a bigger temple.

events.text: Cha Soyul has written a scripture for the temples of terror: a book of rules for being passed over by the Star. Do not be proud. Do not be noticed. Light no lamp on the night of the raid. Mortals below are living by it.

effects.log: You pass over every city that keeps the rules. Below, the rules become law.
You pass over a city that kept none. Cha Soyul's scripture is thrown into doubt.

events.text: Cha Soyul is old now, for a mortal, and has been brought to the top of their temple to die. They ask, into the dark, the only question they have ever wanted to ask: "Did you ever hear us?"

effects.log: The whole temple hears your voice, once. Cha Soyul smiles and closes their eyes.
Cha Soyul nods in the silence, as if it were an answer they expected.

events.text: Cha Soyul's successor is not afraid of you. They are angry. They have torn the black tiles from the temple roof and written on the walls: "A god who must be begged is not a god." The temples of terror below are emptying.

effects.log: The temples become schools, in the end. The prayers to you stop. The fear does not.
You pass over the angry priest's city, and over every city that follows them.

events.text: Cha Soyul, the mortal high priest you sent a dream of yourself, has painted what they saw on the wall of the great temple below. The painting is wrong in every detail but one: the eyes. Mortals come from far away to stand in front of them.

choices.text: Visit the painting in a dream

effects.log: You stand in front of your own eyes for an hour. You cannot look away either.
It is covered. The mortals come anyway, and stand in front of the cloth.

events.text: Cha Soyul has begun to dream of you every night, without your sending. They ask nothing in the dreams. They only sit with you, on a stair you do not recognise, and watch heaven together.

effects.log: You sit with a mortal priest every night for twenty years. It is the most company you have had.
The dreams stop. Cha Soyul paints the stair from memory, and does not paint you on it.

events.text: Cha Soyul's last painting is of the stair from the dreams, with two figures on it, seen from behind. The mortals of the temple do not know who the second figure is. Cha Soyul has told them it is whoever is looking.

choices.text: Look at it a long time

effects.log: You look until dawn. You understand what Cha Soyul meant, and are sorry they are gone.
The temple below never burns, in all the wars to come.

events.text: A hero of {sov_world} has been made into a song by its people: the one who stood in the square and told the falling star to stop. In the song, the star stops. You remember the night. You were only passing over.

effects.log: You never pass over that square again. The song gets a second verse.
The square empties. The song is still sung, more quietly.

events.text: Two of the domains you hold have begun to quarrel, as domains do when the same god holds both: their weather argues at the border, and the mortals below live in a narrow country where it rains and burns at once.

choices.text: Divide them with a wall of cloud

effects.log: The narrow country below gets a clear sky. It is a very small mercy.
One domain wins. The narrow country below learns to live with it.

events.text: A mortal child below has climbed a mountain to leave a black tile at the highest shrine they could find. On it, in a child's hand: "Not my mother." The tile has come up to you through the clouds like any prayer.

choices.text: Keep the tile, and pass that mountain by

effects.log: That mountain is spared for a thousand years. Nobody below knows why.
The tile lies in your hall. You know it is there.

events.text: {sov_god} writes to you, for the first time since you took {sov_domain}. It is a letter of instructions: how the domain likes its mornings, which festivals it keeps, which worshippers below are old and need more care.

effects.log: {sov_domain} is gentler under you than it was. {sov_god} never writes again, but it is enough.
You run {sov_domain} your own way. It does not like it, but it obeys.

events.text: The people of {sov_world} have begun to send you tribute, unasked: grain and silk and carved stones, carried to the edge of their world and left there. They have heard what the Calamity Star does. They are paying not to find out.

effects.log: You send it back. They are more afraid than before.

choices.text: Accept it, and send back blessings

effects.log: The tribute and the blessings cross each other every year, both sides a little confused.

events.text: A god of the Throne of Storms sends you their weather for a day as a courtesy: their thunder rolls over your sky, their rain washes your stair. It is the custom between neighbours of the Storms. Nobody has ever treated you as a neighbour.

effects.log: Your weather goes to them for a day. It is very dark. They are polite about it.

choices.text: Hold their rain and keep it

effects.log: You keep their weather for a year. The Storms do not ask again.

events.text: Gil Haneul, a junior clerk of the Heavenly Court, has drawn the duty nobody wants: serving the Court's warrants on the Calamity Star. They arrive at your gate with a satchel of them, a century's worth, and a very straight back.

effects.log: You take the satchel. Gil Haneul nearly faints with relief, and bows, and goes.

choices.text: Burn them on the stair in front of the clerk

effects.log: Gil Haneul watches every warrant burn and writes down the time. It is their job.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to read them aloud

effects.log: It takes a day. Gil Haneul's voice gives out by evening, and you send for tea.

events.text: Gil Haneul is back with the next century's warrants. They are older now, and have stopped being afraid of you, which the Court has noticed. "They think I am too soft on the Star," the clerk says. "I told them I only deliver paper."

choices.text: Give them a gift to take back

effects.log: You send a jade brush to the chief judge, with no note. Gil Haneul is promoted, to everyone's confusion.
"I cannot," says Gil Haneul. "Someone has to. I would rather it was me."

events.text: The Court has written a warrant it does not mean to serve: one for Gil Haneul, for consorting with the Calamity Star. The clerk brings it to you themselves. "I thought you should see what you have done to my career," they say, almost laughing.

choices.text: Go to the Court and speak for them

ok.log: The judges tear the warrant up. They do not want the Star in the Court twice.

fail.log: The judges hear you and keep the warrant. Gil Haneul is sent to the archive, which they say they prefer.

effects.log: Gil Haneul becomes the only clerk in heaven who serves the Star. Ryu Gaon is jealous.

events.text: Gil Haneul has kept a copy of every warrant ever served on you, a whole archive of them. It is, they say, the most complete history of your path in heaven, written entirely by your enemies, and they want to give it to the Book of Fates.

effects.log: The Book of Fates takes the archive. The page with your name on it grows very long.

choices.text: Ask them to give it to Ryu Gaon instead

effects.log: Ryu Gaon and Gil Haneul argue about the archive for a hundred years, happily.

events.text: You hold a post in the Heavenly Court and raid the domains of gods the Court protects. Your colleagues at the Court have found a solution that saves face: they sit you at the far end of the bench, and pretend not to see your host on the horizon.
events.arc: A Seat in the Court of a Star

choices.text: Use the post to shield a raided god

effects.log: You pass a ruling for {sov_god}. The Court is stunned. So is {sov_god}.

choices.text: Use the post to sign your own warrants

effects.log: You sign three warrants against yourself, as a joke. The Court does not laugh.

choices.text: Sit quietly at the end of the bench

effects.log: You sit and listen for a century. You learn more about heaven than in any raid.

events.text: The Court has a case before it: a minor god accused of raiding a neighbour's domain, in your style. The judges look at you. They are waiting to see whether a Calamity Star will judge someone for being a calamity.
events.arc: A Seat in the Court of a Star

choices.text: Judge them as the law says

effects.log: You sentence them as the law says. Heaven does not know whether to call it justice.
You leave the bench for the case. The judges are relieved and disappointed at once.
The minor god walks free. Every small calamity in heaven takes note.

events.text: The Court asks you to give up your post, very politely, in a letter signed by every judge. It is not a warrant. It is the first time in the Court's history it has asked a god for anything.
events.arc: A Seat in the Court of a Star

effects.log: You set down the post. The judges bow as you leave, all of them.
You keep it. The Court learns to work around a seat it cannot empty.

events.text: An exile of the Heavenly Court has come to your gate, because no other gate in heaven will open to them. They were a judge once, and they wrote warrants against you. "I have nowhere else," they say, "and you are the only god the Court fears more than me."

effects.log: The old judge takes a room above your vault. They sleep for a month.
They go. Somewhere in heaven, a door closes on them for the last time.

events.text: The exiled judge has begun to give your host lessons in the law of heaven: what a warrant may do and may not, what the Book of Fates can write and what it cannot. Mak Dohyeon sits at the back and takes notes.

effects.log: Your next raid is perfectly legal. The Court has never been so angry.

choices.text: Ask them for your own case

effects.log: The judge reads you your case from memory. It is longer than you thought.

events.text: The Court has pardoned the exiled judge, on one condition: that they leave the Calamity Star's sky and never return. The judge packs slowly. "I could stay," they say. "I find that I would rather be pardoned. Is that cowardice?"

effects.log: They go home to the Court. Their first ruling is very fair to a minor god you once raided.
They stay. The pardon is torn up. They never leave your sky again.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has forged a seal of the kind used on corrupt gods, with your name cut into the stone. It is kept in the Court's deepest vault until the Book of Fates writes the word. Ryu Gaon learned of it from a drunk clerk.
events.arc: The Seal That Was Meant for You

effects.log: Your host takes it from the vault in a single night. The Court is mortified.

choices.text: Let it wait in its vault

effects.log: The seal waits. So do you.

choices.text: Send the Court a second stone, blank

effects.log: The Court receives a blank seal-stone with your mark on its box. Nobody knows what it means.

events.text: The seal you stole sits in your hall, cut with your name. At night the letters glow, very faintly, as though the stone is still trying to do what it was made for. Ryu Gaon says a seal that is never used grows hungry.
events.arc: The Seal That Was Meant for You

ok.log: It breaks into nine pieces. Each piece still has one letter of your name.

fail.log: It will not break. It only glows a little brighter, and you sleep badly.

choices.text: Use it on a corrupt god you know of

effects.log: You seal a god the Court never caught. The seal is quiet after that.

events.text: The Book of Fates has written the word. The Court's sealers come for you with the stone from the vault: nine of them, chanting, the seal carried between them on poles like a palanquin. They have never sealed anyone this strong.
events.arc: The Seal That Was Meant for You

ok.log: One sealer falters, and the chant falls apart, and the seal goes home unused.

fail.log: The chant holds for a moment and your power dims for a decade before it breaks.

effects.log: The seal touches you and goes dark. It was made for a corrupt god. You are not one, only a calamity.

events.text: The Court has given up on sealing you. Its sealers have been sent back to sealing the gods they were trained for, and one of them, the youngest, writes to you: "I am glad it did not work. I would not have known what to do with heaven afterwards."
events.arc: The Seal That Was Meant for You

effects.log: You write one line. The young sealer keeps it all their life.

choices.text: Send them the stolen seal, or its pieces

effects.log: The sealers have their stone back. They never use it.

events.text: {sov_war_a} and {sov_war_b} are at war, and both have sent envoys to your gate on the same morning, each with the same offer: march on the other, and keep whatever you take. The envoys have been told to wait in separate rooms. They can hear each other.

effects.log: You march, and {sov_war_b} breaks before you. Heaven calls {sov_war_a} the victor, and you the price.
You march, and {sov_war_a} breaks before you. {sov_war_b} wins a war it will never be proud of.
You strip the rear of both armies in a night. The war pauses, so both sides can hate you together.

events.text: The side you marched for has won, and wants to forget you were ever part of it. Their victory hymns do not mention the Calamity Star. Their envoy brings your share of the spoils at the far edge of your sky and will not come closer.

choices.text: Accept the share and the silence

effects.log: You take it. The hymns stay silent about you. Heaven knows anyway.
You walk into the feast uninvited. Nobody sings for the rest of the night.

events.text: {sov_war_a} and {sov_war_b} have signed a peace, and its first article is about you: neither side will ever again treat with the Calamity Star. Its second article is that they will march together against you, if you march on either.

ok.log: You march on one, and the other does not come. The treaty breaks, and so does the peace.

fail.log: They come together, and you are driven back for the first time in a century.

effects.log: The peace holds for a thousand years. They say it is the only good thing you ever caused.

events.text: The War in Heaven is over. The war-gods of both sides, weary, come together to your gate to ask a question of the god who fed on it: "Will you let the next one start without you?"

effects.log: They go home lighter. When the next war comes, you are not in it.
They go home knowing the next war will have a third side.

events.text: A great battle of the War in Heaven has ended on an open cloud between {sov_war_a} and {sov_war_b}, and neither side has come back for its fallen banners or its broken chariots of light. Your host stands at the edge of the field, waiting for your word.

effects.log: Your host strips the field to the bare cloud. Both sides learn of it and hate you equally.
You bury every banner of both sides in the cloud, with the same rites. Nobody asked you to.

events.text: The war-gods of both sides have learned that the Calamity Star buried their banners. They do not know what to make of it. A herald of {sov_war_a} asks, stiffly, whether the rites were their own or those of {sov_war_b}.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: the same for both

effects.log: The herald goes very still. Then they go home and say it aloud in their own hall.
"Then the banners belong to you now," the herald says, and leaves before you can answer.

events.text: On the field where you buried the banners, something has grown: a meadow of white grass, the only one in heaven. Soldiers of both sides come to it now, on leave, and sit there without armour, not speaking to each other.

effects.log: The meadow spreads a little every year. You never walk on it.
The soldiers stand when they see you, all of them, both sides together.

events.text: The Thrones of heaven are at war, and {sov_realm} has emptied its own halls to fight. Its treasure-houses are guarded by old servants and children. Mak Dohyeon has drawn up a plan. It is a very good plan.

effects.log: {sov_realm} comes home from its war to find its halls bare. The war does not stop, but it changes.
Mak Dohyeon watches it burn and says, "I thought so." The marshal does not seem disappointed.

events.text: {sov_realm}'s servants and children, who guarded its empty halls, have heard that the Calamity Star chose not to come. One of the children has sent a drawing up through the clouds: a star, with a wall in front of it, and the child behind the wall.

effects.log: It is pinned in your hall next to Oh Sanggil's maps. Nobody dares to mention it.
The child gets a small wooden star. They keep it on the wall of the hall they guarded.

events.text: The war of the Thrones is over, and {sov_realm} has lost it, partly because of what you took. Its fallen rulers come to your gate with nothing left to bargain. "Give us one thing back," they say. "Not the treasure. The throne itself. We need somewhere to sit."

effects.log: They carry it home on their shoulders, very slowly, and sit on it in an empty hall.

choices.text: Keep it on your empty cloud

effects.log: It joins the other thrones you have taken, on the cloud where the gods can see it.

events.text: The Concord of Domains, the old meeting of every god who holds a domain, has called a session to decide what to do about you. You hold domains. By its oldest rule you have a seat at it, and a vote, on yourself.
events.arc: The Concord Meets on the Star

effects.log: You sit in the Concord. Every god in the hall moves their chair a little further away.

choices.text: Send Ryu Gaon to vote for you

effects.log: Ryu Gaon votes with great dignity and is not allowed to speak.
The Concord votes without you. Nobody is sure afterward what they decided.

events.text: The Concord's vote on the Calamity Star stands at a tie. Yours is the last vote to be cast. The whole hall waits to see whether you will vote to bind yourself, or to free yourself, or something nobody has thought of.
events.arc: The Concord Meets on the Star

effects.log: You bind yourself by the Concord's law: no domain may be raided at its festival. You keep it.
The motion fails. The Concord has never been so united in silence.
The tie stands. By the oldest rule, a tie means nothing changes. You knew that.

events.text: The Concord of Domains meets again a century later, and the first item is not you. It is a dispute between two harvest gods over a river below. You sit in your seat through the whole of it. Nobody looks at you once.
events.arc: The Concord Meets on the Star

effects.log: You speak for the mortals below the river. Both harvest gods are shocked into agreeing.
It is the first session of the Concord you have sat through as nobody in particular. It is restful.

events.text: An invitation arrives written in ink you can only read in the dark: the Court of the Unlit Sun, heaven's court of shadows, where gods meet who are not supposed to meet. It wants the Calamity Star at its table, once.
events.arc: An Invitation from the Unlit Sun

effects.log: You go down into the dark. The table is long and nobody's face is lit.
The invitation will not burn in daylight. It burns at night, slowly, and smells of nothing.

events.text: At the table of the Unlit Sun, a voice you do not know asks you to raid a domain of its choosing. It names the god. It is one of the most loved gods in heaven. "Nobody would ever believe we asked," the voice says. "They will only believe you did it."
events.arc: An Invitation from the Unlit Sun

choices.text: Refuse, and say so in daylight

effects.log: You tell the whole of heaven what was asked. The Unlit Sun is never quite as dark again.
You keep the secret. The Unlit Sun owes you something now. You do not know what.
You do it. Heaven believes exactly what the voice said it would.

events.text: A second invitation in dark ink. The Court of the Unlit Sun wishes to know whether the Calamity Star would care to sit at its table not as a guest but as one of them. Ryu Gaon reads it by a shuttered lamp and says, "That is the last door in heaven."
events.arc: An Invitation from the Unlit Sun

effects.log: You send back a lit candle. The invitations stop.
The invitation waits in a dark drawer. It is still waiting, a thousand years on.

events.text: Ryu Gaon has bribed a clerk to copy the page of the Book of Fates with your name on it. It is mostly empty. In the margin, in a hand that is not the Book's, someone has written: "Wait."

effects.log: You wait. Nothing comes of it that you can see.
You write a single word. The next copy shows it has been crossed out.

events.text: A warrant has come in red ink, which the Court uses only once an age. It does not name a crime. It names a day, a thousand years from now. Ryu Gaon has put it in the ledger at the right page.

effects.log: The day is marked. You will see it come, or not.
It comes back again. Red warrants cannot be returned.

events.text: A widow of the War in Heaven walks to your border, a god of a small domain whose partner fell on the field. They do not blame you; you were not in the battle. They want to know if a Calamity Star knows how to stop being angry.

choices.text: Tell them how you do it

effects.log: You tell them. It is a very short answer, and they take it home.
They nod, as if that were an answer too, and go.

events.text: A corrupt god the Court sealed long ago has been sealed in a stone near your border, and the stone has begun to speak to you at night. It offers you its whole domain, if you crack it open. It says the Court only fears you because you are honest.

effects.log: The stone talks for a year and then stops, sulking.

choices.text: Move the stone further from your border

effects.log: It talks to someone else now. You hear, later, that they listened.

events.text: Your seat at the Concord of Domains has been carved, as every seat is, with the sign of your first domain. Someone has added a second carving under it, very small: a star with a crack through the middle.

effects.log: The crack stays. Every new god of the Concord asks about it.
It is smoothed away. It comes back by the next session.

events.text: The great bell of the Heavenly Court rings once whenever a Calamity Star raids a domain. It rang so often in your first centuries that the clerks stopped looking up. This year it has not rung at all.

effects.log: The clerks look up when the year ends silent. The Court's bell has been oiled for nothing.
It rings. The clerks look up.

events.text: Dokgo Seon, the Second Star, has come to your hall to plan a raid together. They are younger than you and much louder, and they talk with their hands, and they have brought a map of a domain that neither of you could take alone.

effects.log: You plan it all night. Dokgo Seon's ideas are reckless and three of them are brilliant.
Dokgo Seon talks until dawn. You learn exactly how they think, which may be useful later.

events.text: The joint raid of two Calamity Stars. Your host and Dokgo Seon's go in from opposite sides of the domain at the same hour, and the domain's god, caught between two stars, simply sits down on their throne and waits for whichever of you arrives first.

ok.log: You are first. Dokgo Seon arrives an hour later, laughing, and lets you have it.

fail.log: Dokgo Seon is first, and sits on the throne, and waves at you.

choices.text: Hold back, and let them have it

effects.log: Dokgo Seon takes the domain and never forgets you gave it to them.

events.text: Dokgo Seon has begun to raid domains you told them to leave alone: the small ones, the ones with old gods and few worshippers. When you ask why, they shrug. "Because you would not," the Second Star says. "Somebody should prove you can."

effects.log: You stand at the gate of the next small domain. Dokgo Seon turns their host around, furious.
The small domains of heaven fall one by one. They are not yours to save, you tell yourself.

events.text: The Second Star has come to say goodbye. They are leaving to raid the far edges of heaven, past the Thrones, where nobody has gone. "One sky is too small for two of us," Dokgo Seon says. "I am the one who is going. You can thank me later."

effects.log: Dokgo Seon grins and goes. You never see them again, only hear of them, now and then, very far away.
They go with a thousand of your captains. Your sky is quieter. Heaven's edges are not.

events.text: You ended the Second Star's host in a night, but not the Second Star. Dokgo Seon has been found living in a cave of cloud below the domains with a dozen captains who stayed. They send no challenge. They send only the cup you kept, back to them, broken.
events.arc: The Ash of the Second Star

effects.log: You go alone. Dokgo Seon is sitting by a small fire and does not get up.
The broken cup sits in your hall. Dokgo Seon lives in the cave for a thousand years.

events.text: By the fire in the cave, Dokgo Seon talks for a long time. They became a Calamity Star because of you, they say. They heard the stories as a minor god and thought: there is a god who does not ask. "Then you asked," they say. "You asked me to stop."
events.arc: The Ash of the Second Star

choices.text: Tell them to start again, elsewhere

effects.log: Dokgo Seon goes far away and raids the gods of the outer clouds. Some of them deserved it.

choices.text: Tell them there is another path

effects.log: Dokgo Seon laughs, and then does not, and asks you what it is.

events.text: Dokgo Seon has given up being a Calamity Star. They have become a minor god of a small, unimportant domain: lost things. Below, mortals who lose their keys pray to them. They write to tell you they find it surprisingly hard.
events.arc: The Ash of the Second Star

effects.log: You advise the god of lost things. They find a mortal's lost dog the next day, and write to say so.

choices.text: Lose something, so they can find it

effects.log: You lose a cup from your table. It comes back the next morning, mended.

events.text: Word comes from the far edges of heaven: Dokgo Seon, the Second Star, has been brought down by a league of gods out there, and is held in a ring of fire on an outer cloud. They have asked their captors for one thing: to send word to you.

effects.log: You set out for the far edge of heaven with your host behind you.
You do not go. The far edges of heaven grow quiet again.

events.text: The gods of the outer clouds who hold Dokgo Seon have never seen a Calamity Star of the old heaven. They meet you at the edge of their cloud with their hands open. "We will give them to you," they say, "if you take them home and keep them there."

effects.log: Dokgo Seon comes home with you in silence. They live in your sky the rest of their days, and raid nothing.

ok.log: You break the ring and take them. The outer clouds learn the old heaven's name.

fail.log: The ring holds against you. You go home without them, and wounded.

events.text: Dokgo Seon, old now, sits on your wall in the evenings and watches the gods of heaven go about their business. "They are all so slow," they say. "I used to think that was weakness." They do not finish the thought, and you do not ask them to.

effects.log: You sit with the Second Star every evening for a century. It is the closest thing to a friend either of you has.

choices.text: Ask them to finish the thought

effects.log: "It is patience," Dokgo Seon says. "Which we never had."

events.text: The child you brought home from the ash of {sov_isle} will not speak. Ha Yeonu sits in a corner of your hall with their back to the wall and watches everyone, and when a captain tried to give them a sweet they bit the captain too.
events.arc: The Child Who Bit the Star

choices.text: Sit in the corner opposite them

effects.log: You sit opposite the child for a day. At the end of it, they throw a pebble at you. It is a start.

choices.text: Give them to Ryu Gaon to raise

effects.log: Ryu Gaon teaches the child to read in a month. They still will not speak to you.

events.text: Ha Yeonu speaks for the first time, at ten years old, at your table, in front of the whole host. "You burned my house," they say, very clearly. The host goes silent. The child is waiting to see what you will do.
events.arc: The Child Who Bit the Star

effects.log: Ha Yeonu nods. They eat their rice. They never bite anyone again.

choices.text: Tell them they live here now

effects.log: Ha Yeonu looks at you a long time and says, "For now."

events.text: Ha Yeonu has started following the host on raids, hiding in the supply wagons. Mak Dohyeon has caught them three times. The fourth time, the marshal brings them to you. "They want to see," Mak Dohyeon says. "I think they have a right to."
events.arc: The Child Who Bit the Star

effects.log: Ha Yeonu watches the whole raid from a hill. They say nothing for a month afterward.
They stay home, furious, and learn the forms of the host by watching through a window.

events.text: Ha Yeonu is grown. They have ascended to godhood young, faster than anyone in your host, and on the day of it they came first to you. "I am not grateful," they say. "I wanted you to know I am not. And I wanted you to be the first to see."
events.arc: The Child Who Bit the Star

effects.log: Ha Yeonu looks away. When they look back, they are almost smiling.
Ha Yeonu nods, once, the way you do. You see it, and so do they.

events.text: Your heir, Ha Yeonu, has asked to lead a raid on their own, to learn. They have chosen the domain. It is the one whose god raided {sov_isle} long ago, before you ever did. Ha Yeonu has been reading the old ledgers.

effects.log: Ha Yeonu leads the host, and takes the domain, and gives the spoils to the isle.
You ride at their side and give no orders. Ha Yeonu gives them all, and they are good.

events.text: Ha Yeonu's host is not yours. It raids less and holds more, and its captains are mostly gods of raided isles who came to serve the Little Star. Your old captains grumble. Ha Yeonu says, "A star that only burns, burns out."

choices.text: Agree with them in front of the host

effects.log: Your old captains go quiet. Some of them go over to Ha Yeonu.
You lead a raid of the old kind. Ha Yeonu watches, and takes notes, and does not change.

events.text: Ha Yeonu asks you to tell them, once, without the ledger, why you chose the Calamity Star. They have read everything. They have heard every story. "I want it from you," your heir says. "I am going to have to tell my own heir one day."

effects.log: You tell them. Ha Yeonu listens to the end without interrupting, and then says, "Thank you."
Ha Yeonu does not believe you, and is kind enough not to say so.

events.text: Ha Yeonu, who walked out of your sky when you told them a star has no heir, has been seen in the Green Assembly. They have joined a pantheon, which you never could, and are a minor god of mending things. The Assembly loves them.

effects.log: You go to the border of the Assembly. Ha Yeonu comes out to meet you and does not invite you in.
You stay away. Ha Yeonu does too.

events.text: At the border of the Green Assembly, Ha Yeonu and you talk for an hour across a line neither of you will cross. They have mended three domains you broke. "Not because of you," they say. "Because they needed mending. You were only the reason."

effects.log: Ha Yeonu does not answer. They do not walk away either, for a long time.

choices.text: Ask them to mend one more

effects.log: You name a domain. Ha Yeonu sighs and says, "Already started."

events.text: Ha Yeonu sends you a parcel from the Green Assembly: a small broken cup from your own hall, the one Dokgo Seon gave you or one like it, mended with gold in every crack. There is no letter. It holds tea better than it did before.

effects.log: You drink from the mended cup every morning. It is the only thing in your sky that was ever repaired.
You send the black ledger. It comes back a year later with a new cover, and nothing else changed.

events.text: Your order's disciples have learned what their founder has become. Some are proud. Some are afraid. At the founding feast this year, half the tables are empty: the disciples who left sent their cups back, unbroken, to show they meant no insult.

choices.text: Let them go with your blessing

effects.log: You bless the ones who left. A few come back the next year.

choices.text: Fill the tables with your host

effects.log: Your captains sit at the disciples' tables. The feast is loud and very strange.

events.text: One of the disciples who left your sect has founded a small school of their own on an isle, teaching your forms with every raid taken out. Students come from all over to learn the founder's art without the founder.

effects.log: You watch from the back. The forms are yours, and gentler, and you do not hate it.

choices.text: Send them the forms you never taught

effects.log: You send three forms you kept back. The school becomes famous.

events.text: Your order's youngest disciples have never known a founder who was not a Calamity Star. They have made up a rite: before every raid they light a lamp for the domain you are about to take, and leave it burning until you come home.

effects.log: You stand among them as the lamps are lit. One of them is for a domain you had not decided on.
They stop. The lamps go out, and the disciples watch you leave in the dark.

events.text: Your order has grown into something you did not plan: a house that takes in the immortals of the isles you raid. Half of its elders now are from places your host has burned. They teach your forms and keep your rules and do not forgive you.

choices.text: Let it be what it is

effects.log: It becomes the largest house of the isles. Nobody understands how.

choices.text: Ask the elders why they stay

effects.log: "Because you taught us not to be afraid," one says. "By being the thing we were afraid of."

events.text: Jin Raon, the best disciple of your order, has asked to join your host. They are gifted, serious and very young, and they want to raid. "I want to be you," they say. They mean it as the highest thing a disciple can say.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Asks to March

effects.log: Jin Raon marches with your host. They are good at it, too good.
Jin Raon is stunned, and then angry, and then, after a decade, grateful.

events.text: Jin Raon has taken their first domain, alone, against orders. It was a small domain with an old god who did not fight. Jin Raon brings you the god's seal and waits for praise.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Asks to March

effects.log: Jin Raon carries the seal back and kneels to the old god. They are never quite the same after.
Jin Raon glows. Your host has a second calamity in it now.

events.text: Jin Raon comes back to your order a hundred years later, a teacher now, and asks to speak to the disciples about the Calamity Star. They have asked you to stand at the back and say nothing, whatever they say.
events.arc: The Disciple Who Asks to March

effects.log: Jin Raon tells them everything. At the end, they turn and bow to you, and you bow back.
Jin Raon talks anyway, and you hear about it, every word.

events.text: You dream of a Calamity Star a thousand years after you, raiding domains that do not exist yet. In the dream you cannot see their face, only that they hold their sword the way you taught somebody once.

effects.log: You wake before you can. The way they held the sword stays with you.
They turn, in the dream, and you wake. You do not know if they heard.

events.text: The disciples of your order leave a lamp burning at the gate whenever you are away on a raid. One of them has stayed up every night for a year to keep it lit. They are asleep beside it when you come home.

choices.text: Let them sleep, and keep it lit yourself

effects.log: You keep the lamp lit till dawn. They wake ashamed. You say nothing.

choices.text: Wake them with a word of thanks

effects.log: They wake to the Calamity Star thanking them, and do not sleep again for a week.

events.text: The youngest captain in your host has led their first raid, and done it beautifully, and come home and been sick behind the stable. Mak Dohyeon has found them. The marshal asks whether you want to see them.

effects.log: You tell the young captain it was the same for you. It was not. It is still the right thing to say.

choices.text: Send them to Baek Yuhwa's house of stopping

effects.log: The captain goes, and does not come back to the host. You do not blame them.

events.text: There is a rumour in the markets of heaven of a Calamity Star in the outer clouds, beyond the Thrones, that raids nobody: it only goes to domains that are about to fall to some other god, and stands at the gate.

choices.text: Send someone to find out who

effects.log: They come back a year later. Nobody knows. The star never gives a name.
It is better as a rumour. You let it stay one.

events.text: A letter from Ha Yeonu arrives on your stair. It contains only a list of the domains they have mended this century, with the names of the gods who live in them now. At the bottom: "Your turn."

effects.log: You mend a single small domain, badly. Ha Yeonu's next letter has it on the list, with a note: good.

choices.text: Send back a list of your own

effects.log: Your list is of domains you took. Ha Yeonu sends it back with half of them marked: next.

events.text: Captains of your host have had children, as gods sometimes do, and the children have grown up in your sky. They play at raiding in the courtyard, one side the host, the other side the gods. Nobody wants to be the gods.

effects.log: You let a dozen children take your domain in the courtyard. They are merciless.

choices.text: Tell them the gods win sometimes

effects.log: The children are outraged. One of them asks when. You have to think.

events.text: An elder of the Lineage of Ash and Morning comes to your hall, older than the pantheons and not shy about it. "We were here when the first fire was lit," they say. "We have seen nine Calamity Stars. We would like to see the end of the tenth, and write it down."
events.arc: The Lineage That Saw the First Fire

effects.log: The elder takes a seat in the corner of your hall and stays there, taking notes in a very old script.

choices.text: Tell them there will be no end to see

effects.log: The elder writes that down too, with a small smile.

events.text: The elder of Ash and Morning reads you what they wrote of the nine Stars before you. Each one ended differently: one was sealed, one made peace, one became a pantheon of their own, one simply walked out of heaven and was not seen again.
events.arc: The Lineage That Saw the First Fire

effects.log: "The one who walked out," the elder says. "Nobody ever learned why."
"That is what I am here to find out," the elder says, and goes back to the corner.

events.text: The elder of Ash and Morning is packing up. They have stayed in your corner for three centuries and seen enough. "You are not like the nine," they say. "I cannot tell you how. I have written it down as best I can. You may read it when I am gone."
events.arc: The Lineage That Saw the First Fire

effects.log: You read it before they reach your gate. It is three lines. You keep them to yourself.
The account stays sealed in your vault. You think about it often.

events.text: The Lineage of the Long Tide marries into every pantheon and belongs to none, and now, for the first time in its long history, it offers a match to a Calamity Star: one of its young sea gods, to bind your host to its waters.
events.arc: A Match from the Long Tide

effects.log: They come, and are very calm, and are not afraid of you, which surprises you both.
The Long Tide is not offended. It has been refused before, by older gods than you.

events.text: The young sea god of the Long Tide has spent a year in your sky. They do not love you; nobody loves a Calamity Star. But they like the quiet of your hall, and they have begun to tell you about the deep currents of heaven, which no pantheon knows.
events.arc: A Match from the Long Tide

choices.text: Let the match go on as a friendship

effects.log: The Long Tide accepts it. Your host never raids a domain by the sea again.
They go home with a gift of starlight and a good word. The Long Tide remembers.

events.text: The Long Tide sends word: its young god has married into the Throne of Storms after all, and the Lineage wishes you to know that their first child is to be named after the quiet of your hall. It is a word in the sea tongue nobody else speaks.
events.arc: A Match from the Long Tide

choices.text: Send a gift for the child

effects.log: You send a small pearl from your vault. The Long Tide is very pleased.
It means the hour before a storm. Of course it does.

events.text: The Lineage of the Unlit Lamp keeps the oldest records of heaven and lends them to nobody. Tonight a lamp with no flame is set on your stair. Ryu Gaon knows the sign: the Lamp will show you one record, once, if you come in the dark.
events.arc: The Records of the Unlit Lamp

effects.log: You walk to the Lamp's halls without a light. They are waiting for you at the door.

choices.text: Leave the lamp on the stair

effects.log: In the morning it is gone. The Lamp does not ask twice.

events.text: The record the Unlit Lamp shows you is the ledger of the first Calamity Star, from before the pantheons. It is very short. The first page says: "I am afraid." The last page says the same thing, in a much steadier hand.
events.arc: The Records of the Unlit Lamp

effects.log: They refuse, and then let Ryu Gaon copy the first line only. It goes into your ledger.
"Everything," the keeper says. "As with you."

events.text: The Unlit Lamp has asked for your ledger, to keep when you are gone. They have never asked a god for a record before; they take them, or they wait. "We would rather have it given," their keeper says. "It reads better given."
events.arc: The Records of the Unlit Lamp

effects.log: The Lamp writes your promise down in the dark. It is the only promise of yours they keep.
"Nothing goes with anyone," the keeper says, kindly.

events.text: The keeper of the Unlit Lamp comes to check that the ledger is still kept. They turn the pages without reading them, by touch. At the end they say, "There is a page missing." There is not. They mean the one you have not written.
events.arc: The Records of the Unlit Lamp

choices.text: Write it now, in the dark

effects.log: You write in the dark. The keeper does not look. You do not know what you wrote until morning.

choices.text: Tell them it will be written

effects.log: "By whom?" the keeper asks, and goes.

events.text: The Lineage of the Root is owed a great deal by everyone, and now by you: every domain you took grew on their deep earth. Their factor comes with a scroll of the debt. It is very long, and very patient, and it charges no interest.

effects.log: You put your seal to it. The factor bows. The Root has never had a Calamity Star's seal.

choices.text: Tell them the Star pays nobody

effects.log: The factor rolls up the scroll. "We can wait," they say. They can.

events.text: The Root asks for its first payment, after a hundred years: not starlight, not a domain. A single root of your oldest tree, to plant in their deep earth. "So we have something of yours that grows," the factor says.

effects.log: They plant it in the dark of the deep earth. Ryu Gaon says it is the strangest bargain in the ledger.

choices.text: Ask for the debt to be forgiven instead

ok.log: The Root forgives half. Nobody has ever got that much.

fail.log: The Root forgives nothing, and smiles, and keeps waiting.

events.text: The root you gave has grown in the deep earth into something nobody expected: a tree that grows downward, into the dark under heaven. The Root sends you a cutting. "It is yours, too," the factor says. "Debts grow. So do the things that pay them."

effects.log: It grows down through your clouds, slowly. The mortals below see a dark root in the sky.

choices.text: Send it back to the deep earth

effects.log: It goes back. The Root writes: debt paid. It is the first time they have written that.

events.text: The Dao Ancestor, who stands at the top of the road, has turned their eyes on heaven for the first time in an age. Every god feels it. Your host feels it most: the Ancestor is looking at the Calamity Star.

effects.log: You look up. For a moment, the top of the road looks back at you, and you are very small.
You raid as if nobody is looking. Heaven thinks you are very brave or very foolish.

events.text: The Dao Ancestor has come down, as they come down perhaps once an age, and sits at the foot of your stair. They are smaller than you imagined, and very old, and they ask you a single question: "What did you take that was worth it?"

effects.log: You answer. The Ancestor nods slowly, as if your answer were one they had heard before.
The Ancestor laughs, which shakes the clouds, and does not answer.

events.text: The Dao Ancestor rises from your stair to go back up the road. Before they go they touch your host's war-banner, very lightly, and the colours fade a little. "Not a punishment," they say. "A reminder. Colours fade. That is all."

effects.log: Your host marches under a paler banner. Heaven reads it as a sign.
The new colours are bright. They fade again in a century.

events.text: The Dao Ancestor's descent has changed heaven a little. The gods talk of nothing else for a century, and some of them have begun to come to your stair to sit where the Ancestor sat, in case something is left there.

effects.log: They sit, and look up the road, and go home. Your stair is a shrine now.
You sit. Nothing is left there but the view.

events.text: Pyo Jaeun, keeper of the Clone Forge, has refused to forge a clone of a Calamity Star for anyone in heaven. Now someone has offered them a domain to do it. Pyo Jaeun has come to you to ask, quite simply, what you would do in their place.
events.arc: Pyo Jaeun of the Clone Forge

effects.log: Pyo Jaeun refuses the domain. The god who offered it does not forgive either of you.
Pyo Jaeun takes the domain and forges nothing. They are a better liar than they look.

events.text: Somewhere in heaven, someone has forged a clone of you anyway, with a lesser forge. It has raided a small domain in your colours, very badly. Pyo Jaeun has come to say it is not theirs, and to offer to help you find it.
events.arc: Pyo Jaeun of the Clone Forge

ok.log: You find it in a hollow cloud, confused and frightened. It looks like you, young.

fail.log: It slips away from you twice. The third time, it is gone into the outer clouds.

effects.log: It raids two more domains and stops on its own. Nobody knows what it became.

events.text: Pyo Jaeun has found the clone of you: an echo of the soul grown badly, sitting in a hollow cloud, asking everyone it meets what it is for. Pyo Jaeun says a clone can be unmade, gently, back into the forge's fire. Or it can be kept.
events.arc: Pyo Jaeun of the Clone Forge

effects.log: It goes into the fire without fear. It thanks you before it goes. You were not expecting that.
It stays in your sky, a smaller you, and learns slowly not to raid.

events.text: The Heavenly Calendar has its great gatherings: games, contests, feasts of the gods. The Calamity Star is barred from all of them by an old rule. This year a young contestant has protested the rule, publicly, because they want to fight you.

choices.text: Accept their challenge, outside the Calendar

effects.log: You meet them on an open cloud. They are very good, and very young.
The rule stands. The young contestant wins the whole gathering, out of spite.

events.text: The young contestant you fought outside the Calendar has become a champion of every gathering in heaven. At each victory they turn to the empty seat where the Calamity Star would sit, and bow. The organisers hate it.

choices.text: Come and sit in the seat once

effects.log: You sit in the seat for a single gathering. Nobody stops you. The champion bows to your face.
They keep bowing. It has become part of their style.

events.text: The Heavenly Calendar has changed its rule. A Calamity Star may now attend the gatherings, as a spectator, unarmed. The new rule has a name, after the champion who bowed. You are the only one it applies to.

effects.log: You sit in the stands of a festival of heaven. The gods around you do not watch the games.
The rule stands, unused. It is still on the Calendar's books a thousand years later.

events.text: The Tower that runs up through every world has floors for the gods, and one of them, very high, has been sealed since before the pantheons. Its door carries a sign nobody can read. Ryu Gaon has read it. It says: for the Star.

effects.log: You climb the Tower's divine floors, past gods who press against the walls to let you pass.
The door stays shut. You find yourself thinking about it at odd hours.

events.text: Behind the sealed door of the Tower's floor is a single room with a single chair and, on the wall, the marks of nine other Calamity Stars who sat here: a scratch each, at the height of a hand. There is room on the wall for one more.

effects.log: You make your scratch. It is a little lower than the others. You were sitting down.
You sit for a day. When you leave, the room is as it was.

events.text: Gods have started climbing the Tower to see the floor kept for calamities. They are mostly young, and mostly disappointed: it is only a room. One of them has written under the scratches, very small: "Is that all?"

effects.log: You write: yes. Someone writes under it: thank you.
The door closes. The young gods go back to the lower floors.

events.text: Your Dao has changed. A god's Dao grows with what they do, and you have done one thing for a long time. When you sit to meditate, your Dao no longer reaches out. It only takes, very quietly, from everything near.

effects.log: You follow your Dao into the dark of taking. You come back stronger, and colder.
It takes a century of sitting still. Your Dao gives a little, grudgingly, like a miser.

events.text: Your Dao of taking has reached the end of what it can take. When you meditate now there is nothing at the bottom, a well with no water, and the stillness there is the deepest you have ever felt.

effects.log: You stay a decade. When you rise, the stars near your sky are brighter.
You come up shaken. You will not go down there again soon.

events.text: Your Dao, turned outward, has begun to give in ways you cannot control. The domains you took grow richer under you. Their mortals below have good harvests. Your host is bewildered. You are a calamity that brings rain.

effects.log: You let it. The terror of your name grows thinner below, and thicker in heaven.
The rain stops. Your Dao sulks. So do you.

events.text: The Elder Lineages gossip about you. You know because a servant of the Lineage of the Root left a letter behind in your hall by mistake: the Lineages are arguing over how your path will end. The Root says peace.

choices.text: Send the letter back with a note

effects.log: You write: so am I. The Root frames it.
You read it every few years. The arguments change.

events.text: You dream of the top of the road, where the Dao Ancestor stands. In the dream you are climbing, and the Calamity Star is a heavy thing on your back, like a sack of stones. Every step you take, you drop one.

effects.log: You wake light and strange. Your host thinks you are ill for a week.
You wake tired. The stones are still on your back, and still yours.

events.text: On the night of the Heavenly Calendar's great feast, the gods of heaven send up lanterns, one each. Someone has sent up one in your colours. Nobody will say who.

effects.log: It rises with the rest. You watch it all the way up.
It goes dark mid-sky. A hundred gods see it fall.

events.text: A spark from the Clone Forge drifts into your sky: a seed of a soul, waiting to be forged. Pyo Jaeun sends word that it has your shape, and asks you to send it back before someone uses it.

effects.log: It goes back to the forge. Pyo Jaeun puts it out, gently.
It glows in a lamp on your table. It never grows. It never goes out.

events.text: When you walk, the grass of heaven bends away from you. It always did, a little. Now it bends away for a whole pace before you reach it, and stays bent after, as if remembering. Your Dao has become a shape in the world.

effects.log: It takes a century to learn. Then the grass only bends as you pass.
Heaven learns your path by the grass. It is easier to stay out of your way.

events.text: A god who climbs the Tower's divine floors every century stops at your floor, the one kept for calamities, and leaves a cup of tea on the chair, as if you might come. Ryu Gaon says they have done it for three hundred years.

effects.log: You drink it, cold. The god never learns, and keeps leaving it.

choices.text: Leave a cup for them on their floor

effects.log: They find it and climb down very quickly. The tea stops after that.

events.text: Among the captives of {sov_domain} is the heir of {sov_god}, a young god who was to inherit the domain you took. They are kept in a room of your vault, and they have not eaten in a month. They are not protesting. They are simply waiting to fade.
events.arc: The Heir of the Fallen Domain

effects.log: You sit with the heir until they eat a single plum. It takes a day.
The heir goes home to a parent without a domain. Neither of them thanks you.
They fade, in the end, slowly. {sov_god} never forgives it, and heaven never forgets.

events.text: The heir of {sov_god} eats now, and reads, and has asked for the run of your library. They are clever and very angry, and they have started writing a history of {sov_domain} from before you came, so that somebody remembers it as it was.
events.arc: The Heir of the Fallen Domain

effects.log: The heir reads every book you took from {sov_domain} and copies them out by hand.

choices.text: Give them back the domain's own archive

effects.log: You hand them the archive of {sov_domain}. The heir weeps over it in private.

events.text: The heir of {sov_god} has finished their history. It is brilliant and fair, and it ends with your raid, which it describes exactly. They want to send it to every pantheon of heaven. They have asked your permission, which they did not need to.
events.arc: The Heir of the Fallen Domain

effects.log: The history goes out. Heaven reads it and understands you a little better, and likes you no more.

choices.text: Ask them to add one page

effects.log: You tell them one thing about the raid nobody knows. They add it. The history is better.

events.text: The heir of {sov_god} has asked to leave. They are a god in their own right now, and a historian, and the Unlit Lamp has offered them a seat among its keepers. "I hated you for a long time," they say. "I do not now. That is not forgiveness. It is tiredness."
events.arc: The Heir of the Fallen Domain

choices.text: Let them go with a gift

effects.log: You give them the domain's crown of names. They take it without a word.

choices.text: Ask them to stay as your archivist

effects.log: They refuse, gently. Ryu Gaon is relieved.

events.text: In the raid on {sov_domain}, a temple below burned: a mortal temple to {sov_god}, struck by a falling shard of their domain as it broke. Its priests have gathered in the ash and are praying, to nobody now. The prayers come up to you, because you hold the domain.

effects.log: You send rain to put out the last of the fire. The priests do not know whom to thank.
The prayers go on for a year, and then stop.

events.text: The mortals below are rebuilding the burned temple, in stone this time, with a new name over the door. They do not know your name, only that the god who took their temple's god sent rain. They have named it the Temple of the Rain After.

effects.log: The temple below stands for a thousand years. It is famous for its gardens.

choices.text: Let it stand on its own

effects.log: It stands, unblessed. Mortals pray there anyway, as mortals do.

events.text: The Temple of the Rain After has a priest who has dreamed of you: not the Calamity Star, only a god with tired eyes who sent rain once. They have carved your face from the dream over the altar. It is the kindest face anyone has ever given you.

effects.log: You stand before the carving. It is not you. You wish it were.

choices.text: Send the priest a dream: it is not me

effects.log: The priest wakes and does not change the carving. Faith, they write, is not about who.

events.text: The vault of {sov_domain} will not open for you. It answers only to the god who made it, and {sov_god} has refused. Your host has tried every key and every array. The door simply waits.
events.arc: The Vault That Would Not Open

effects.log: You post a guard on a door that will not open. It becomes a joke in your host.

ok.log: It breaks. Inside is a single painting of a young god holding a child. Nothing else.

fail.log: It does not break. Your hands ache for a year.

events.text: {sov_god} has written to you. The vault holds nothing of worth to anyone but them, they say, and they will tell you what it is if you promise not to open it. "It is the only thing I did not let you take," they write. "Let me keep that."
events.arc: The Vault That Would Not Open

effects.log: You promise. {sov_god} writes back to tell you what it is. You keep the promise, and their secret.

choices.text: Tell them you will open it one day

effects.log: {sov_god} does not write again. The guard on the door is doubled, by them, from outside.

events.text: The door of the vault of {sov_domain} has opened by itself. {sov_god} must have died, or given up, or forgiven you. Inside is a painting of a young god holding a child. The child is {sov_god}. The young god is nobody heaven remembers.
events.arc: The Vault That Would Not Open

choices.text: Close it again and seal it

effects.log: You seal the vault. Nobody will open it while you hold the domain.
It goes to them. They hang it in a small house in exile.

events.text: Your host has brought back hostages from {sov_isle}: twelve young immortals, children of its elders, to keep the isle from striking back. They sit in a row in your hall in their best robes, very straight, very scared, and none of them cries.

effects.log: The hostages are given rooms and tutors and are not allowed to leave. They are very confused.
They are kept under guard in a tower. The isle sends no hunters for a decade.
They walk home over the cloud bridges. The isle does not understand you at all.

events.text: The twelve hostages of {sov_isle} have grown up in your sky. They have learned your host's songs and Ryu Gaon's arithmetic and Mak Dohyeon's spear. One of them has asked to stay when the others go home.

effects.log: They stay. In a century they are one of your captains.
All twelve go home. The one who asked to stay looks back the whole way.

events.text: One of the hostages in the tower has tried to escape, and fallen from the cloud. They live, badly hurt, caught in a net of the isle's own arrays below your sky. {sov_isle} has seen it, and is gathering at its edge.

choices.text: Bring them up and heal them

effects.log: You heal the hostage yourself. The isle stands down. Nobody speaks of it again.

choices.text: Let the isle take them home

effects.log: The isle takes them. It takes the other eleven, too, that night, by force. You let it.

events.text: The hostages of {sov_isle} are elders of the isle now. They meet once a century, the twelve of them, in a tea-house nobody else is allowed into, and Ryu Gaon has learned that they spend the whole evening talking about you.

choices.text: Ask Ryu Gaon what they say

effects.log: They say you were fair, and that it was the worst thing about you.
You never ask. You hear, much later, that they always leave an empty chair.

events.text: A raid has broken against the guard of a domain of the Green Assembly. Your host is coming home in pieces, and one captain did not come home at all: Kang Byeol, who has served you for three hundred years, is held in the Assembly's roots.

effects.log: You go back over the border alone, at night.
The Assembly asks a domain for Kang Byeol. You pay it. Heaven is astonished.
Kang Byeol stays in the roots. Your host does not forget it.

events.text: The roots of the Green Assembly hold Kang Byeol gently, like a seed. The Assembly's warden finds you there before you can cut them free. "We are not hurting them," the warden says. "We are only asking them to stop. Will you let us?"

ok.log: The roots let go. Kang Byeol comes home with you, and is never quite a raider again.

fail.log: The roots hold you too, for a night. In the morning the warden lets you both go.

effects.log: You wait a year. Kang Byeol comes out of the roots on their own, and goes home to plant a garden.

events.text: Kang Byeol has written to you from the garden they planted. The roots of the Green Assembly taught them something, they say, and it was not to stop raiding. It was how slow a thing can be and still win.

choices.text: Ask them to teach it to the host

effects.log: Kang Byeol teaches the host patience. Your raids grow slower and harder to stop.
They stay in the garden. It grows into a wood.

events.text: On the night march to a domain of the Throne of Storms, one of your captains simply sits down by the road and will not get up. They are not afraid, they tell Mak Dohyeon. They are done. They want to see what happens if they do not go.
events.arc: The Captain Who Did Not March

effects.log: The host marches past. The captain is still sitting there at dawn when you return.
They get up and march. They raid well. They never sit down again, and never speak of it.

events.text: The captain who sat down by the road is still there, a year later, living in a hut of cloud at the edge of your road. Other captains stop to talk to them on the way to raids. Some of them sit down too, for an hour, and then go on.
events.arc: The Captain Who Did Not March

effects.log: You sit by the road for an hour. Your whole host stands behind you, waiting.
You march past. The captain watches you go and raises a hand.

events.text: The hut by the road has become a place: an inn of sorts, where gods on the march stop to sit and be done for a while. Gods of other pantheons come to it. Even the Righteous Immortals stop there, on the way to hunt you.
events.arc: The Captain Who Did Not March

effects.log: It is the only place in heaven where your host and your hunters drink at the same table.

choices.text: Visit it once, as a guest

effects.log: The innkeeper, your old captain, pours for you and charges you, like anyone.

events.text: The isles of the immortals are joined by bridges of cloud, ancient and fine. In your raid on {sov_isle}, your host cut every bridge to it, and the isle has hung alone in the cloud-sea since, reached only by flying, which its old and its young cannot do.

effects.log: You spin one bridge back yourself. The old of the isle cross it first, slowly.
{sov_isle} hangs alone. Its old do not see their families for a century.

events.text: The one bridge you rebuilt to {sov_isle} is the busiest in the cloud-sea. The isle has hung a lantern at each end of it, and on the lanterns, in the isle's script, a word Ryu Gaon translates as: owed.

effects.log: You rebuild every bridge. The lanterns stay on the first one, only.
One bridge. One lantern at each end. It is enough, or it is not.

events.text: A child of {sov_isle} crosses your bridge every day to a school on the next isle. Today they stop in the middle and look up at your sky and wave. Nobody has ever waved at the Calamity Star.

effects.log: The child runs the rest of the way, shrieking. They will tell everyone. Nobody will believe them.
The child waves every day for a year, and then grows up and stops.

events.text: The ash of the domains you raid does not stay in heaven. It falls, slowly, through the clouds to the world below, and in one mortal country it has fallen for a century. Its fields are grey. Its people call it the Star's snow.

effects.log: You shift your raids. The grey snow below stops.
The country below learns to farm in ash. Its crops are strange and very hardy.

events.text: The mortals of the grey country below have found that the ash of the gods makes their soil rich. Their harvests are the best in their world. They have begun, very quietly, to pray for more raids.

effects.log: The ash stops for good. The country goes back to ordinary harvests, and ordinary prayers.

choices.text: Send them the ash of your vault

effects.log: You send it down. Their harvests are rich. Their prayers are strange.

events.text: A scholar below has written a book about the Star's snow: where it came from, which gods it was, what it did to the soil. It is mostly wrong. Its last chapter is a prayer to the snow itself. Mortals of the grey country read it at weddings.

effects.log: It goes on being read at weddings for a thousand years.

choices.text: Send the scholar a true dream

effects.log: The scholar writes a second book. Nobody reads it at weddings.

events.text: The cloud where you leave the thrones of the gods you threw down is crowded now. Eleven thrones stand on it, at odd angles, each still carrying the shape of the god who sat in it. The gods of heaven see it every morning.

effects.log: The thrones stand in a ring, facing in, like a council of the gone.
They stand at odd angles. It is worse, somehow, than a ring.

events.text: Gods have started going to the cloud of thrones at night to sit in them. Not to claim them: only to sit. Ryu Gaon has seen {sov_god} sit in their own old throne for a whole night and then get up and leave.

effects.log: The cloud becomes a place where fallen gods sit and remember. You never go there at night.
The guard turns them away. They stand at the edge of the cloud instead, and look.

events.text: One of the thrones on the cloud has cracked and fallen in a storm. The god it belonged to, long gone, has no heirs. Mak Dohyeon asks whether to clear the pieces away or leave them where they lie.

effects.log: The cairn stands at the edge of the cloud. Gods leave small stones on it.
The cloud has one empty place now. Nobody fills it.

events.text: The dawn after a raid. Your host is quiet, as it always is, and the domain you took is quiet, and somewhere a bird of heaven that does not know anything has happened is singing on the broken gate.

effects.log: You stand on the gate and listen until it flies away.
The host marches. The bird keeps singing behind you.

events.text: Ryu Gaon has counted the spoils of the last raid three times, and each time the count is one short. It is a small thing: a jade comb. Somebody in the host has kept it.

effects.log: Ryu Gaon makes a note. The count is one short forever.
A young captain took it for someone below. You let them send it.

events.text: On every isle you have raided, the immortals plant a single grey flower where the gate stood. Your host has started to recognise the flowers from the air: a grey dot for every gate you broke.

effects.log: Ryu Gaon counts. It is a very long garden.

choices.text: Avoid the isles with the flower

effects.log: Your host avoids them. The flowers become a ward nobody planned.

events.text: In the ash of a raided domain your host finds a half-burned letter, never sent, from its god to someone in another pantheon. The half that survived says: "If the Star comes, I will not run. I want you to know that."

choices.text: Send it to the one it was for

effects.log: You find them. They read it and thank you, and hate you for the rest of their life.
It sits in the ledger between two raids. You read it more than once.

events.text: A god you mean to raid next has sent their whole treasury to your gate before you can march, with a note: "Take it, and leave the domain." It is a fortune. It is everything they have.

choices.text: Take it and leave them be

effects.log: You take it. The god lives on in an empty domain, and is the happiest god in heaven.

choices.text: Send it back and march anyway

effects.log: You march. They had nothing left to defend with. Heaven does not forgive this one.

choices.text: Send it back and do not march

effects.log: You send it all back. The god does not understand. Nobody does.

events.text: In the burned orchard of a raided domain, a single seed has survived, black and hard. Your gardener says it is from a tree that only grows in ash.

effects.log: It grows into a black tree with silver leaves. It flowers on the anniversary of the raid.

choices.text: Plant it where the orchard was

effects.log: It grows there alone, in the ash, and in a century there is an orchard again.

events.text: A mortal-born immortal of the isles saw your last raid from a hill and has written a poem about it. The poem is being copied all over the isles. It does not call you a monster. It calls you weather.

effects.log: You read it twice. It is the truest thing anyone has written about you.
You cannot stop a poem. It is in every hall by spring.

events.text: A god whose domain you took has sent you a gift on the anniversary of the raid: a small box of earth from the domain as it was before. Inside the lid is written: "So you remember what it smelled like."

effects.log: Every year you open the box. Every year it smells less like anything.
The god keeps it unopened, too. Neither of you will smell it again.

events.text: Ryu Gaon's hand has begun to shake. The ledger's lines wander now, and twice this year they have written a raid in the wrong century. They have not said anything. They only hold the pen a little tighter every morning.
events.arc: The Last Pages of Ryu Gaon

effects.log: You write. Ryu Gaon reads over your shoulder and corrects you, gently, every line.

choices.text: Let them write, wandering lines and all

effects.log: The ledger wanders. You never correct it. Ryu Gaon notices, and is grateful.

events.text: Ryu Gaon asks for a holiday, the first in all their service. They want to see the domains in the ledger, the ones they wrote down and never visited. "I want to know what they look like," they say. "I only ever knew how they were spelt."
events.arc: The Last Pages of Ryu Gaon

effects.log: You travel heaven together for a year. Ryu Gaon makes notes on everything, out of habit.
Ryu Gaon goes with a dozen captains and comes back sunburnt and very happy.

events.text: Ryu Gaon is dying, as gods sometimes do when they have done one thing for long enough. They lie in a room next to the ledger, because they asked to. "Read me the first page," they say. "Whatever is on it. I want to hear it in your voice."
events.arc: The Last Pages of Ryu Gaon

effects.log: You read the first page aloud. Ryu Gaon closes their eyes and smiles at the end of it.

choices.text: Read them the green book instead

effects.log: You read the thin green book of things you did not destroy. They fall asleep before the end.

events.text: Ryu Gaon is gone. The ledger lies closed on its stand. Nobody in your host can read the old script it is written in, except you, and you were never the one who wrote it. The pen is still where they left it.
events.arc: The Last Pages of Ryu Gaon

effects.log: You write the next entry. Your hand is worse than theirs. It will have to do.
You close it. From now on, nothing you do is written down. Heaven notices at once.

choices.text: Give it to the Unlit Lamp

effects.log: The Lamp takes it in the dark. You write nothing after that, and remember everything.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol, once envoy of the Silent Hall, has offered to be yours. "Nobody bargains for a Calamity Star," they say. "That is exactly why it would work. They will not know what to expect."

effects.log: Yun Hwaseol takes up a staff in your colours. They still will not sit.
They nod, and do not ask again. They do go on visiting.
