events.text: Yun Hwaseol has come back from the Will of Heaven with a treaty no Calamity Star has ever been offered: a festival-peace. One week a year, your host may walk the markets of heaven unarmed, and no market may close to it.

effects.log: Your host walks the markets of heaven for a week. The merchants are terrified, and then, slowly, are not.
Yun Hwaseol goes back and gets a month. They come home exhausted and pleased.

events.text: Yun Hwaseol is old now, and has finally sat down, in a chair in your hall, and has not got up for a week. "I said I would stay too long if I sat," they say. "I was right. I want you to know I was right about everything."

effects.log: Yun Hwaseol laughs, and stays another week, and then goes home to the Silent Hall to rest.

choices.text: Bring them tea and say nothing

effects.log: They drink it. They stay. It is a good chair.

events.text: Every market in heaven shuts when your shadow crosses it. Every stall but one: Mun Sejin, who sells ink and paper in the Will of Heaven's great market, keeps their shutter up and goes on serving whoever is in front of them.

effects.log: You buy a stick of ink. Mun Sejin wraps it properly and gives you your change.
Mun Sejin does not look up. You find you are grateful for that.

events.text: The other merchants of the great market have complained about Mun Sejin to the market's god: a stall that stays open to the Calamity Star brings the Star. Mun Sejin has been told to close when you come, or leave.

effects.log: You walk in and speak quietly. Mun Sejin's stall stays open. The other merchants say nothing more.
You stop going. Mun Sejin keeps their stall open anyway, every day, just in case.

events.text: Mun Sejin has written to you. They sell ink, they say, and you have bought a great deal of it, and they have worked out from the amount roughly how much you write. "It is a lot," they say. "I hope some of it is letters."

effects.log: You write Mun Sejin a letter. It is the first you have written in a century that is not an order.

choices.text: Buy more ink, and say nothing

effects.log: They wrap it as always. There is a small blank card in the parcel, for a letter.

events.text: Mun Sejin has died, very old, at their stall. Their child keeps the stall now, and on the first day you come, they keep the shutter up, as their parent did. Their hands shake while they wrap your ink. They do not drop it.

effects.log: They nod. The great market watches the Star buy ink, and goes on with its day.

choices.text: Pay for a year in advance

effects.log: They put the money in a box marked with your colours, and never spend it.

events.text: In the pantheons of heaven, gods tell their children: eat your rice, or the Calamity Star will come. A child god of the Green Assembly, Ahn Dami, has decided to find out if it is true, and has run away to your gate with a bowl of uneaten rice.
events.arc: The Name Heaven Frightens Children With

effects.log: Ahn Dami walks into your hall and puts the bowl down on your table, watching you. You eat the rice.
Ahn Dami goes home and tells everyone the Star would not even see them. It is worse, somehow.

events.text: Ahn Dami's parents have come for their child, white with fear. Ahn Dami does not want to go. "The Star ate my rice," they tell their parents. "That means it cannot come for me now. That is the rule."
events.arc: The Name Heaven Frightens Children With

choices.text: Agree that it is the rule

effects.log: The parents take Ahn Dami home. The rule spreads through the Green Assembly in a month.

choices.text: Tell them there are no rules

effects.log: Ahn Dami looks at you a long time and decides you are lying.

events.text: The children of the Green Assembly no longer fear the Calamity Star at dinner: they leave a spoonful of rice on the windowsill for it, and then it cannot come. Ahn Dami, grown, has become a minor god of the Assembly. They still leave the spoonful.
events.arc: The Name Heaven Frightens Children With

choices.text: Never raid a house with rice on the sill

effects.log: You never do. The Assembly's children grow up knowing they were right.

choices.text: Raid one, to break the rule

effects.log: You do. The rule breaks. The children are frightened again, and so is Ahn Dami.

events.text: Nobody who marched in your first host is still in it. The founders have faded or gone home or died, one by one, over three thousand years. The captains now know your first raids only as stories, and some of the stories are wrong.

effects.log: You tell your host the first raids as they happened. They are shorter and worse than the stories.
The host keeps its stories. They are better than the truth, and they march better on them.

events.text: The young captains have made a pilgrimage to the place of your first raid. It is a small domain, rebuilt now, whose god does not remember you. They come back puzzled. "It was so small," one says. "Why did you start there?"

effects.log: You tell them. It was a very small reason. They respect you more for it, oddly.

choices.text: Tell them every star starts small

effects.log: They nod as if it were wisdom. You are not sure it was.

events.text: A new captain asks you, at the founding feast, whether you are tired. Nobody has ever asked you that. The whole hall goes silent, and the captain realises what they have done, and does not take it back.

effects.log: The hall stays silent. Then, one by one, the oldest captains nod.

choices.text: Tell them a star does not tire

effects.log: The captain bows. The feast goes on. You go to bed early.

events.text: Your host has grown into a thing of its own, older than any pantheon's army. It does not need your orders to march. Some years it goes out without you and comes back with spoils, and the gods of heaven do not know it was not you.

choices.text: Let it go on without you

effects.log: Your host raids under your colours for a century while you sit. It is your name it carries, not you.

choices.text: Call it home and hold it

effects.log: It comes home. It stays. It is restless, and so are you.

events.text: The wounds heaven's waves gave you have begun to ache, all at once, at the hour when the stars change watch. Your physician says a god's wounds remember the hand that gave them, and some of those hands have gone below and been born mortal.

effects.log: You find one, far below: an old farmer whose shoulder aches at the same hour as yours.
You bear it every night at that hour. Your host learns not to speak to you then.

events.text: The old farmer below whose shoulder aches when yours does has no memory of heaven. Their village has a story about them, though: that in a former life they fought a star, and lost, and that is why they plant at night.

choices.text: Send them a dream of the fight

effects.log: They dream it, and wake, and plant at dawn for the first time.
You ease it below, and yours eases too. A god's wound can be healed from the other side, it turns out.

events.text: The aches have gone quiet one by one, as the mortals who were once the waves live out their lives below. Only one remains, in your side, from the last wave. It does not ache. It only waits.

effects.log: It waits. So do you.

choices.text: Ask the Silent Hall whose it is

effects.log: They tell you. It belongs to someone who is not dead.

events.text: You dream that you are mortal, below, with a small house and a field and no host. In the dream nobody is afraid of you. A neighbour borrows your hoe. You wake with the weight of it still in your hands.
events.arc: The Dream of a Mortal Life

effects.log: You find the dream again the next night. The neighbour returns the hoe.

choices.text: Wake your host for a march

effects.log: You march before dawn. The weight of the hoe does not leave.

events.text: The dream of the mortal life has gone on for years now, a night at a time. In it you have married no one, raised no one, and grown old in a field. Your neighbour has died. You went to the funeral, in the dream, and wept.
events.arc: The Dream of a Mortal Life

effects.log: You keep the dream. It is the only life you have where nobody counts.
You end the dream. The field below, which was never real, goes fallow.

events.text: In the dream of your mortal life, you are dying, old and content, in the small house. The last thing you see is the sky, and in it, very bright, a star you do not recognise. You wake. You know exactly whose it was.
events.arc: The Dream of a Mortal Life

effects.log: You sit on your stair until noon. Your host does not disturb you.
You tell no one. You never dream of the field again.

events.text: An oracle of the Silent Hall, Gong Seoha, has dreamed the end of the Calamity Star, and has come to tell you before they tell anyone else. "It is only fair," they say. "You are in it."
events.arc: The Oracle of the Star's End

effects.log: Gong Seoha tells you. It is not what you expected. It is not a battle.
Gong Seoha nods. "Then I will not tell anyone," they say. They keep their word.

events.text: The end Gong Seoha dreamed for you was a quiet morning in an empty hall. Since they told you, you have caught yourself looking at your hall on quiet mornings, counting who is there.
events.arc: The Oracle of the Star's End

effects.log: You keep the hall full of captains and guests and noise. The mornings are never quiet.
You sit alone in your hall at dawn, often. It is not as bad as you feared.

events.text: Gong Seoha, who would not tell anyone your end, has been asked by the Heavenly Court to tell it, under oath. They have refused, and the Court has threatened their seat. They have not asked for your help.
events.arc: The Oracle of the Star's End

choices.text: Go to the Court and release them

ok.log: You tell the Court you release Gong Seoha from their silence. They still say nothing.

fail.log: The Court will not hear the Star. Gong Seoha loses their seat, and keeps their silence.

effects.log: Gong Seoha keeps it. The Court lets them be, in the end, out of embarrassment.

events.text: Gong Seoha has dreamed again. The end they saw for you has changed. They come to say so, and only that. "I do not know what you did," they say. "But it is not the same morning."
events.arc: The Oracle of the Star's End

effects.log: They tell you. You laugh, for the first time in a long time.
You thank them. Whatever it is, it is yours to find.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon's old spear still stands in your hall where the marshal set it down. A young captain has asked to carry it on a raid. Nobody else has ever dared to ask.

effects.log: They carry it and come home with it unbroken, and set it back exactly as it was.
It stays where it is. The young captain is relieved, a little.

events.text: The Heavenly Court's offices close for the day whenever you are seen in the street of the archives. Clerks lock their doors and pull the shutters. Today one forgot, and is sitting very still at their desk, pretending to be furniture.

effects.log: The clerk breathes again an hour later. They tell nobody.
They give you one, shaking. You fill it out properly.

events.text: Ryu Gaon, or whoever now keeps the ledger, has worked it out: you are the oldest Calamity Star heaven has had. The nine before you all ended sooner. Nobody knows what happens to a star this old.

effects.log: You go on. That is all there is to do.
The Lamp has no record. It is very interested in you now.

events.text: In the Will of Heaven they have begun to say "the Star" instead of your name, the way mortals below say "the old one" for a bear. A herald of theirs slipped and said your real name in a speech, and the hall went silent.

choices.text: Send them a note: it is all right

effects.log: The herald keeps the note. Your name comes back into use, slowly.
Nobody says your name again for a century.

events.text: The stars near your sky that dimmed for you in your first centuries are almost all bright again. They came back while you were not looking. The sky around a Calamity Star, it turns out, forgets.

effects.log: You let it. The sky is beautiful, and you are in it.
They dim, slowly, one by one. It is harder than it used to be.

events.text: Moss has grown on your gate. Nobody has knocked on it in a hundred years, and nobody has dared to scrape it off. It is very green.

effects.log: It grows into a carpet. Birds of heaven nest in it.

choices.text: Have it scraped and open the gate

effects.log: Your gate is open. Three gods knock in the first year, very nervously.

events.text: A captain has found out the day you became a god, three thousand years ago, and has told the host. The host has made a cake. It is a terrible cake. They are all waiting.

effects.log: You eat a slice in front of everyone. It is worse than it looks. The host cheers.
The captain steps forward, terrified. You make them eat the first slice.

events.text: Every oracle of heaven has seen the same omen this year: a star falling upward. They all agree it is about you. They all disagree about what it means.

effects.log: "It means you will stop falling," they say. "Or that you never were."
The omen comes again the next year, and the next. You never learn what it meant.

events.text: The halls of the Will of Heaven cast no shadows: its gods rule by being seen. Mak Dohyeon has found a way in. "Bring a shadow," the marshal says. "Where there is none, one is enough. They will not know what it is."
events.arc: The Halls That Cast No Shadow

effects.log: You walk the shadowless halls as the only dark thing in them. The gods of the Will cannot see you at all.
They see you coming for a day. The raid is long, and loud, and you win it.

events.text: Since your raid the halls of the Will of Heaven have shadows: small ones, in corners, that will not go away. The gods there look at them nervously. A young god of the Sky has started sitting in one, to read, because it is cool.
events.arc: The Halls That Cast No Shadow

effects.log: The Will of Heaven learns to live with a little dark. It is gentler for it, a little.
The shadows come back to you. The halls are bright again, and the young god misses their corner.

events.text: The young god of the Sky who read in the shadows has written to you. They have started a school in the Will of Heaven for gods who like to sit in the dark. It has nine students. They want to know if you would send them one more shadow.
events.arc: The Halls That Cast No Shadow

effects.log: A shadow arrives at the school in a box. The students name it.
You send them the shadow you cast. You do not cast one for a year after.

events.text: Nobody hears the gods of the Silent Hall arrive. Your host, raiding a domain of the Hall, finds itself suddenly surrounded by them, standing perfectly still in a ring, as if they had always been there.

ok.log: The ring breaks. The gods of the Hall step back without a sound and are gone.

fail.log: The ring holds. Your host goes home in silence, and nobody speaks for a week.

effects.log: You stand as still as they do, for a day. At dusk, the ring bows, and lets you go.

events.text: The Silent Hall has begun to send one of its gods to stand in your hall once a decade, unannounced, unheard. Your captains find them in corners at dawn. They do nothing. They are, Yun Hwaseol says, keeping you company in the only way the Hall knows.

effects.log: You stand in silence with a god of the Hall each decade. It becomes a kind of friendship.
They stop. Your hall feels very loud after.

events.text: A god of the Silent Hall has spoken in your hall, for the first time in a century of standing. A single word, in the old tongue. Ryu Gaon's successor looks it up. It is the word the Hall uses for a god who has stopped being a stranger.

effects.log: You find the word for it. The god of the Hall smiles, and is gone.
Silence is the Hall's answer too. They understand.

events.text: You raid a domain of the Green Assembly, the oldest gods, who rule by growing. The domain falls easily. In the morning, everything you burned has begun to grow back, a little, from the roots.

effects.log: You burn it again. It grows again. It is going to be a long war.
You leave the domain to the Assembly. Its gods watch you go, very calm.

events.text: The domain of the Green Assembly has grown back three times, and three times your host has burned it. Its god sits in the middle of the ash, unhurried. "We can do this for a long time," they say. "Can you?"

effects.log: You stop. The Assembly never boasts of it. It only grows.

ok.log: The fourth fire is the one it does not grow back from. The Assembly mourns quietly.

fail.log: It grows back by noon. Your host is very tired.

events.text: The Green Assembly has sent you a seedling, in a pot, with no note. Yun Hwaseol says it is the Assembly's way of saying that it has decided you are a season. It will wait you out.

effects.log: It grows in your garden, slowly. The Assembly hears, and nods.
It grows in the pot until it breaks it. The Assembly is pleased about that too.

events.text: The gods of the Throne of Storms argue in weather. When you raid a domain of theirs, they argue about what to do about you, and for a week the skies below rain hail and lightning and snow all at once.

effects.log: They decide, after a week, to do nothing. The weather below clears.
You take the domain in a hailstorm. The Storms do not forgive it.

events.text: The Throne of Storms has sent its answer to your raid: not an army, a single cloud, which follows your host wherever it goes and rains on it. Mak Dohyeon says it is the most effective weapon anyone has used against you in a thousand years.

effects.log: You argue back in weather. The cloud gives up and rains on the sea.
Your host marches in the rain for a century. It grows used to it. So do you.

events.text: The cloud the Storms sent to rain on your host has grown fond of it. When the Storms called it home, it would not go. It hangs over your sky now, raining softly on your garden, and the Storms are embarrassed.

effects.log: Your garden has never been greener. The Storms stop sending clouds.
It goes home, sulking, and rains on the Throne of Storms for a year.

events.text: A god of a small domain on your border has sent you their youngest child as a ward, in the old way: a hostage of good faith, so you will not raid them. The child is Seo Ari, and has brought a bag of books and a very serious face.
events.arc: The Ward Sent to the Star

effects.log: Seo Ari gets a room, a tutor and a seat at your table. They read through dinner.

choices.text: Send them home with a promise

effects.log: You send Seo Ari home and promise not to raid their parent. You keep it.

events.text: Seo Ari has been your ward for twenty years and has decided to become a historian of the Calamity Star, since they have the best seat in heaven for it. They interview your captains. They interview you, every winter.
events.arc: The Ward Sent to the Star

effects.log: Seo Ari writes it all down. Their history is famous before it is finished.
Seo Ari writes down what you do not answer, too, and that is the better book.

events.text: Seo Ari's parent has died, and their small domain needs a god. Seo Ari is ready to go home. "I was a hostage," they say. "I want you to know I know that. I also want you to know it was the best house I could have grown up in."
events.arc: The Ward Sent to the Star

choices.text: Let them go with your blessing

effects.log: Seo Ari's domain is never raided, not by you, not by anyone. Heaven knows whose ward they were.

choices.text: Give them a captain to guard it

effects.log: A captain of your host stands at Seo Ari's border for a thousand years.

events.text: The gifts have started coming. Every decade, gods who fear your raid send you something: a jar of first light, a hawk of heaven, a song sung for you alone. Ryu Gaon has had to open a new room. None of the gifts is from anyone you meant to raid.
events.arc: Gifts to Keep the Star Away

effects.log: They come back. The gods who sent them are more frightened than ever.

choices.text: Keep them and raid nobody who gave

effects.log: You keep them. The gift-givers sleep easy. Those who sent nothing do not.

events.text: A god who sent you nothing has come to ask why. They are poor, a god of a very small domain, and they could not afford a gift. "I want to know if I am next," they say. "So I can tell my worshippers."
events.arc: Gifts to Keep the Star Away

effects.log: They go home and tell their worshippers below. Their faith doubles from relief.

choices.text: Ask them for a gift anyway

effects.log: They give you a pebble from their domain. You keep it with the jars of first light.

events.text: The room of gifts is full. Ryu Gaon or whoever keeps the count now has found that the oldest gifts are from gods who no longer exist. Their gifts are all that is left of them in heaven.
events.arc: Gifts to Keep the Star Away

choices.text: Give them to the Unlit Lamp

effects.log: The Lamp keeps them in the dark, with the records. It is a better place than your vault.

choices.text: Keep the room as it is

effects.log: The room stays full. You go in sometimes and sit among the gifts of the gone.

events.text: Below, a band of mortals has taken your name as their banner: they raid their neighbours in the name of the Calamity Star and leave your sign burned into the doors. Their prayers to you are not for mercy. They are for help.
events.arc: The Ones Who Want to Be Like You

effects.log: Their raids go well. The world below fears the Star's followers more than the Star.
Their raids fail one by one. They curse you, and their neighbours pray to you for the first time.
They go on in your name. Below, nobody can tell the difference.

events.text: The followers below whom you helped have become a small country, ruled by a warlord who wears your sign on their chest. They have built you a temple of black stone. They want a sign that you are pleased.
events.arc: The Ones Who Want to Be Like You

effects.log: Lightning strikes the black temple. They take it as a blessing. It was not meant as one.

choices.text: Send them a dream of what you are

effects.log: The warlord wakes and takes off the sign. The country below is very confused.

events.text: The followers below whose luck you turned have scattered. One of them, old now, in the hills, has written you a prayer on the back of their old banner: "I understand now. Thank you for not letting us."
events.arc: The Ones Who Want to Be Like You

effects.log: The old one below lives to a great age and teaches the children of the hills to grow rice.
You keep the banner. It is a better banner than the one they meant.

events.text: A scholar below has traced every band of mortals that ever raided in your name. There have been forty-one in three thousand years. None of them lasted. The scholar has written a book called The Star Does Not Answer.
events.arc: The Ones Who Want to Be Like You

effects.log: The book is read for a thousand years. Fewer mortals raid in your name.
The scholar writes a second edition with a new last chapter. It is called: Usually.

events.text: A great beast of heaven has begun to follow your host: a long grey thing, part serpent, part cloud, that waits outside every domain you raid and feeds on the broken arrays you leave behind. The gods call it the Star's dog.
events.arc: The Beast That Follows the Host

effects.log: You drive it off. It comes back the next raid, a little further away.
You throw it the broken arrays yourself. It follows closer, and begins to guard the host.

events.text: The Star's dog has grown huge on the arrays of the domains you raid. The gods of heaven now fear it more than your host. Horang, Lord of the Wild, or whoever holds Beasts now, has sent word: it is not a beast of any domain. It was born of you.
events.arc: The Beast That Follows the Host

ok.log: It lies down at your gate and lets you put a hand on its head.

fail.log: It will not be tamed. It only waits outside, larger every year.

effects.log: It goes into the outer clouds, slowly, looking back.

events.text: The grey beast that followed your host has died, of age, in the outer clouds. The gods who found it say it had curled up facing your sky. In its belly, undigested, were the arrays of every domain you ever took, still faintly glowing.
events.arc: The Beast That Follows the Host

effects.log: They glow in your vault, a map of everything you broke.

choices.text: Return the arrays to their domains

effects.log: One by one they go home. The domains are stronger for it.

events.text: The domain you stripped to the bedrock long ago has begun to come apart. Not in a storm: quietly, at its edges, like cloth unravelling. A domain left with nothing at all, Ryu Gaon says, forgets that it is a domain.

effects.log: You pour your own power into its edges. The unravelling slows.
It unravels for a century, and then it is a hole in heaven, small and very cold.

events.text: Holding the unravelling domain has cost you. Every century you must go and pour yourself into its edges again. The domain does not thank you. It does not know you. It only knows it is still there.

effects.log: You keep it. It is the only domain in heaven that depends on you for its life.

choices.text: Find it a god of its own

ok.log: A young god takes it on, and it begins, slowly, to remember itself.

fail.log: Nobody will take a domain the Star stripped. You keep holding it.

events.text: Where the domain you let unravel used to be, there is a hole in heaven. Things fall into it. Small gods avoid it. The Heavenly Court has put a fence around it, with your name on a sign, as the god responsible.

effects.log: You take it down. The Court puts it back up. They are right.

choices.text: Stand at the fence a day

effects.log: You stand at the edge of what you did. Gods pass and do not look at you.

events.text: Something has begun to grow at the edge of the unmade place: a single blade of grass, on nothing, where no domain is. The gods of the Green Assembly come to look at it. Nobody can say whose it is.

effects.log: It grows. A second comes up a century later.
You water it. The Assembly sees, and says nothing, and comes back each spring to look.

events.text: A herald of the Will of Heaven reads a proclamation at your border: the Calamity Star is condemned in every hall of the Will, forever. It takes an hour. At the end, the herald asks, very quietly, whether you would like a copy.

effects.log: It arrives on good paper, sealed. Ryu Gaon files it with care.
The herald goes home relieved. The proclamation is read in every hall anyway.

events.text: Two gods of the Throne of Storms have argued for a century, in weather, about whether you will ever raid their domains. The skies below are confused. A herald comes to ask, on behalf of both, whether you have decided.

effects.log: One of them is very pleased. The other sulks in fog for a decade.

choices.text: Tell them you will decide when you arrive

effects.log: The argument goes on. The weather below stays confused.

events.text: A god nobody knows knocks on your gate and asks for a cup of water, nothing else. They drink it on your stair and thank you and walk off into heaven. Your gatekeeper is sure they were someone important.

effects.log: They walk into the Silent Hall and are gone.

choices.text: Leave a cup on the stair in case they return

effects.log: The cup stays on the stair. Someone drinks from it once a century.

events.text: A god of War who fears you has sent you a sword as a gift: the best they ever forged. On the blade they have engraved, very small, a single request: "Not my children."

choices.text: Keep the sword and honour it

effects.log: You keep both. The god's children live long in their domain.

choices.text: Send it back, with the request granted

effects.log: The sword comes home to them. They weep over it.

events.text: A mortal parent below has named their child after you, not out of reverence: so that, they pray, the Star will think the child one of its own and pass them by. The prayer reaches you very small.

effects.log: The child grows up and never knows why everything they fear goes around them.
The child grows up ordinary. The name is a joke in their village below.

events.text: One of the stars you dimmed in your first centuries has not come back. It has gone out altogether. Ryu Gaon's successor says it is the only star in heaven that you are certainly responsible for.

effects.log: You pour power into the cold place. Nothing happens. Then, a century later, a spark.
You give it a name nobody else knows. You say it sometimes.

events.text: The hunters of the isles who come for you now are the grandchildren of the first. They come less angrily than their grandparents did, and more carefully, and they bow before they draw.

effects.log: You bow. They fight better for it, and lose with dignity.
They draw, and lose, and go home, and come back bowing.

events.text: A child god of the Will of Heaven has wandered into your sky on a dare and fallen asleep in your garden. Their parents are at your gate, terrified, with a whole delegation behind them.

effects.log: You carry the sleeping child to the gate. The parents do not breathe until it is in their arms.
The captain carries the child out. The parents never forget whose sky it was.

events.text: The tithe of the four pantheons comes every decade with the same courier: Bang Jiun, a minor god of roads, who carries a decade of starlight on their back in a plain sack and always arrives on time, and always sits on your stair for an hour before going home.

effects.log: You sit on the stair with Bang Jiun for an hour. They talk about roads.
The captain signs for it. Bang Jiun sits on the stair anyway, alone.

events.text: Bang Jiun has been robbed on the road to your sky: a band of minor gods, desperate, who did not know whose starlight it was. They have taken the tithe. Bang Jiun has arrived empty-handed and is waiting for you to decide what that means.

effects.log: You tell the pantheons the tithe was paid. Bang Jiun stares at you for a long time.

ok.log: You find them in a day. They give it back, shaking, and you let them go.

fail.log: They are gone into the outer clouds. The pantheons pay twice that decade, nervously.

events.text: Bang Jiun has carried the tithe for six hundred years and is retiring. They have brought their successor, a young god of roads, to your stair to meet you. "Sit with them," Bang Jiun says. "For an hour. It matters more than the starlight."

effects.log: You sit for an hour. The young courier talks about roads, too, nervously at first.

choices.text: Give Bang Jiun a road of their own

effects.log: You lay a small road of cloud from your stair to nowhere. Bang Jiun walks it every evening.

events.text: The roads of heaven are closed to your host, and your domains have started to run short of things only markets sell: the inks of the Will of Heaven, the threads of the Silent Hall. A smuggler, Yeom Taeil, has offered to bring them in, at a price.

effects.log: Yeom Taeil brings ink and thread through the closed roads by night. Your domains are grateful.
Your domains learn to make their own ink. It is grey and does not last.

events.text: Yeom Taeil has been caught by the gate-wardens of the Throne of Storms with a cart of the Silent Hall's thread bound for your sky. They are standing in the rain at a border, waiting to be made an example of.

ok.log: The warden lets Yeom Taeil go rather than fight the Star at the border.

fail.log: The warden holds, and Yeom Taeil stands in the rain a year. You bring them dry clothes every week.

choices.text: Pay their fine to the Storms

effects.log: The Storms are surprised to be paid by a Calamity Star, and let Yeom Taeil go.

events.text: The roads of heaven have quietly reopened to your host, one by one, without any treaty. A warden of the Storms says only that the rain at the borders was getting expensive. Yeom Taeil, out of work, has asked you for a job.

effects.log: Yeom Taeil becomes your quartermaster. Your host has never been so well supplied.

choices.text: Send them home with a purse

effects.log: Yeom Taeil buys an inn on a road of heaven and names it after the closed years.

events.text: The minor river god who gave up their true name to buy peace still has no name. Their worshippers below pray to "the river" now, and the river answers. Gods of heaven do not know how to address them at feasts, and so do not invite them.

effects.log: They come, and sit at the end of your table, and are addressed as nothing, and do not mind.
You name them. It is not their true name. They thank you and use it anyway.

events.text: The river god without a name has asked you to keep their true name safe, since you are the only one who has it. Someone in the Unlit Sun has offered you a great deal for it. You did not answer.

choices.text: Burn the paper it is written on

effects.log: You burn it. Now nobody has it, not even you. The river god is relieved.
You keep it in your own memory, and nowhere else.

events.text: The river below that the nameless god keeps has become the most peaceful place in the world below. Mortals travel to it to settle their feuds, because, they say, the river has given up something to keep the peace, and so can they.

effects.log: Its waters run clear for a thousand years.
It does not need you. That is the point.

events.text: The first century of your sentence: standing still on a spot of cloud the Court chose, at the edge of your sky. Your host comes every day to ask for orders. You give none. Mak Dohyeon begins to give them instead.

choices.text: Speak to the marshal once a year

effects.log: You give one order a year. It is always the same: do no harm. The host obeys.
You stand in silence. Your host learns to live without you.

events.text: The gods of heaven have begun to visit you where you stand, the way mortals visit a famous statue. They walk around you. Some of them say things to you they would never have dared say before. One of them is {sov_god}.

effects.log: {sov_god} talks for a whole day. When they leave, they bow, very slightly.
{sov_god} stands in front of you until you look back. It takes a year.

events.text: Children of heaven have started climbing you. They are not afraid of a god who cannot move. A small god of the Green Assembly has built a nest on your shoulder for a bird that does not exist yet.

effects.log: The bird comes, in the end. It lays its eggs on your shoulder.
You move a hair's breadth. The Court notes it. The children never come again.

events.text: The last century of your sentence. The judges of the Court come to see you stand, and are surprised to find that the bird on your shoulder has had chicks, and that the chicks have had chicks, and that you are covered in moss.

effects.log: They do not know what to do with thanks. They go home and write it down.
You say nothing. The judges go home and talk about it for a hundred years.

events.text: The judges of the Heavenly Court who heard you read the first page of your ledger have not been the same. Two of them have resigned. One has asked to be posted to the farthest edge of heaven. One has written you a letter asking what the second page says.
events.arc: The Judges Who Heard the Ledger

effects.log: You send it. The judge reads it and does not write again.

choices.text: Tell them there is no second page

effects.log: The judge writes back: then why did you number the first?

events.text: The judge who read the second page of your ledger has started a reform of the Court: every warrant against a god must now be read aloud in front of them, in full, before it is served. It is slow. It is, the clerks say, unexpectedly fair.
events.arc: The Judges Who Heard the Ledger

effects.log: Your support is the worst thing for their reform. They thank you anyway.
The reform passes. Warrants against you are read aloud too, at your gate, for hours.

events.text: The Court has a new chief judge: the one who asked what the second page said. Their first act is to summon you, not for trial. "I want to read you the first page of mine," they say, and do.
events.arc: The Judges Who Heard the Ledger

effects.log: It is short, and terrible, and honest. You understand why they asked.
You leave. The chief judge finishes reading to an empty room.

events.text: You struck the League of the Long Count where it met, and emptied the hall. Not everyone in it was a hunter. A clerk of the League, Pi Yoonseo, was there taking minutes, and has written down everything you did in the hall, in order.
events.arc: Those Who Lived Through the Hall

effects.log: Pi Yoonseo sends them. They are very exact. They do not say anything about you that is not true.
The minutes burn. Pi Yoonseo writes them again from memory.

events.text: Pi Yoonseo has become the League's historian, and the minutes of the struck hall are read aloud at its every meeting. New hunters learn your name from them. They do not learn hate. They learn the order things happened in.
events.arc: Those Who Lived Through the Hall

effects.log: You hear your raid read aloud by someone who was there. You do not stay for the end.
You correct one detail. Pi Yoonseo adds it, with a note: corrected by the Star.

events.text: Pi Yoonseo is very old now and has sent you the last copy of the minutes, bound. "I wrote them so that someone would know," they say. "I have decided that someone should be you."
events.arc: Those Who Lived Through the Hall

effects.log: The minutes and the ledger sit side by side. They tell the same night.

choices.text: Give them back to the League

effects.log: The League keeps them. Pi Yoonseo is buried with a copy.

events.text: The domain you chose to govern rather than strip has wardens now: captains of your host who stayed, married, raised children there. Their children have never raided anything. They have asked you to come to their harvest festival.
events.arc: The Wardens of the Governed Domain

effects.log: You sit at the harvest table among the wardens' children. They pour your tea without spilling.
You send starlight for the festival. The children use it to light lanterns.

events.text: A child of the wardens of your governed domain, grown now, has been elected by the domain's mortals below as their intercessor: the one who carries their prayers up. Their first prayer is that the domain never be raided, even by you.
events.arc: The Wardens of the Governed Domain

effects.log: The domain is safe from you forever. It is the only domain in heaven that is.

choices.text: Tell them it is already granted

effects.log: The intercessor bows. The mortals below light a fire that can be seen from heaven.

events.text: The governed domain has grown so peaceful that gods of other pantheons visit it to see how it is done. Its wardens give the same answer every time: "The Star was here first. After that, nobody else wanted to try."
events.arc: The Wardens of the Governed Domain

effects.log: You laugh when you hear it. Your host hears you laugh, which is rare.

choices.text: Ask them to say something else

effects.log: They say something else. It is worse. They go back to the first answer.

events.text: The question you had written on the first page of your ledger, what is a star for, has started to be answered. Not by you: someone writes an answer under it every few decades, in a different hand each time, and you never see them do it.
events.arc: The Question on the First Page

effects.log: There are three so far. One says: to be seen. One says: to fall. One says: so the night has something in it.
You cover it with a strip of black cloth. The answers keep coming, under the cloth.

events.text: You have found out who writes the answers in your ledger: everyone. Every captain who has served you a hundred years is allowed, by a custom of your host you did not know existed, to write one line under the question on the first page.
events.arc: The Question on the First Page

effects.log: You write your line under theirs. It is the shortest one.

choices.text: Let the custom go on without you

effects.log: The custom goes on. The page fills slowly, and you do not read it again.

events.text: The first page of the ledger is full. There is no more room under the question. Your host has asked what to do. The newest captains are waiting to write their lines.
events.arc: The Question on the First Page

effects.log: The question goes on to a second page. The captains are proud.

choices.text: Write the last answer, and end it

effects.log: You write the last answer. You do not read it to anyone. The custom ends there.

events.text: Your host has learned the Guardians' art of standing still from Baek Yuhwa. In your next raid, the domain's defenders charge, and your host simply stands, and the charge breaks on it like water on a wall. Nobody on your side strikes a blow.
events.arc: The Host That Learned to Stand Still

choices.text: Order no blows in future raids

effects.log: Your host takes domains without striking. Heaven does not know what to make of it.
They strike after the charge breaks. It is quicker. It is also worse.

events.text: A raid with no blows struck. The god of the domain stands in their own hall, unhurt, surrounded by your host, who are simply standing there. They ask you, very puzzled, what happens next.
events.arc: The Host That Learned to Stand Still

effects.log: They leave. You take the domain. Nobody is hurt.

choices.text: Leave them the domain, and go

effects.log: Your host walks out. The god sits down on their own stair, shaking, and laughs.

events.text: Baek Yuhwa has watched your host take a domain without a blow. They come to you afterward. "That is not what I meant to teach them," they say. "I meant to teach them to defend." They are not angry. They are trying to decide what they are.
events.arc: The Host That Learned to Stand Still

choices.text: Tell them it is the same art

effects.log: Baek Yuhwa thinks for a long time and agrees, and does not like it.

choices.text: Promise to use it only to defend

effects.log: You promise. Your host stands still at your borders, and nowhere else.

events.text: A mouse of heaven has been living in the sack of starlight the pantheons send as tithe, and has grown fat and luminous. Your quartermaster found it this morning glowing in the vault.

effects.log: It lives in your vault for a century, lighting the corridors.

choices.text: Send it back with the next courier

effects.log: It goes back to the pantheons, glowing. Nobody there knows what it means.

events.text: The bird that nested on your shoulder during your sentence has come back, long after, and is sitting on your shoulder again. It does not seem to understand that you can move now.

effects.log: You stand still all afternoon. Your host waits.
It rides on your shoulder through the hall. Your captains are very careful not to laugh.

events.text: A young captain was found reading the ledger at night by lamplight, from the beginning. They are only at the second century. They are crying, very quietly.

effects.log: You sit while they read. You do not explain anything. They do not ask you to.
They go to bed. They never open it again. You are not sure that is better.

events.text: A child of the League of the Long Count, carried out of the struck hall as a baby, has grown up and come to your gate. They do not want revenge. They want to see the god who was the reason for everything in their life.

effects.log: They look for a long time. "Smaller," they say, as everyone does.
They tell you. It is a good life. It has you in it, the way weather is in a life.

events.text: Oh Sanggil has written in the margins of the copy of your ledger you sent them, and sent it back: little notes beside every raid. Most of them are corrections of the time of day. One says only: this one was cruel.

effects.log: You read it. They are right.
Oh Sanggil writes back: yes. But that one was cruel.

events.text: The first page of your ledger is still empty, as you ordered. Gods of heaven speak of it the way mortals below speak of an unmarked grave: with a shiver, and a kind of respect.

effects.log: The page stays empty. The shiver stays.

choices.text: Write a single word on it

effects.log: You write one word. Ryu Gaon reads it and says nothing. Heaven never learns it.

events.text: The domain you stripped to the bedrock is the coldest place in heaven. Gods passing over it pull their robes tight. A god of Fire offered once to warm it and was refused by the Court: it is still yours.

choices.text: Let the god of Fire warm it

effects.log: You give leave. A small fire burns on the bedrock. It is something.
It stays cold. It is your warning, and heaven reads it.

events.text: The gods of heaven still cannot always tell whether it is your host or the Second Star's at their gate. Some of them now hang two lanterns at their borders, one for each, and pray to both.

choices.text: Ask Dokgo Seon to fly a different colour

effects.log: Dokgo Seon flies purple. It does not help anyone, but it is festive.
Heaven fears two stars that might be one. It works.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon has set down the spear, and your host needs a marshal. The old marshal has chosen one for you without asking: Cho Haeun, a quiet captain who has never lost a raid and never won one quickly. "They will annoy you," Mak Dohyeon says. "Good."

effects.log: Cho Haeun takes the host. Their first order is to slow the march by a day.
You choose a loud, fast captain. Mak Dohyeon says nothing, very pointedly.

events.text: Cho Haeun asks you, before every raid, a single question: what will the domain be like afterward? Nobody has asked you that before a raid. You have started to know the answer before you march.

effects.log: Some raids you call off because of the answer. Cho Haeun never says anything about it.

choices.text: Tell them it is not their concern

effects.log: Cho Haeun asks anyway, every time, politely.

events.text: Cho Haeun visits Mak Dohyeon's garden once a month to report, as if the old marshal still commanded. You have found out about it, and Cho Haeun is embarrassed. "They know the host better than I do," they say. "I wanted to be good at it."

effects.log: The three of you sit in the garden of arguing plants and talk about the host until dark.
They go on visiting. The host gets better every month.

events.text: The merchants of a great market of heaven have put up a statue of you at the market's gate: not to honour you. A god told them that a Calamity Star will not raid a place where its own face is watching. They polish it every morning.
events.arc: The Statue at the Bazaar Gate

effects.log: You never raid that market. The statue's nose grows shiny from being touched for luck.
The statue watches you raid. The merchants take it down the next day.

events.text: Other markets of heaven have copied the statue of you, and each sculptor got you a little wrong. Some are tall, some fat, one has six arms. Every market has one now. You have never been so famous for your face.
events.arc: The Statue at the Bazaar Gate

effects.log: You stand before it for a while. A child asks if you are the god it is of. You say no.

choices.text: Send a sculptor to get it right

effects.log: The sculptor fixes every statue. The merchants preferred the wrong ones.

events.text: A rival god has raided a market of heaven with your statue at its gate, to prove the statues worthless. The merchants have sent word to you, as if you could do something about it. They seem to expect you to.
events.arc: The Statue at the Bazaar Gate

choices.text: Go and do something about it

ok.log: You return everything the rival took, and the rival with it. The statues are worth something now.

fail.log: The rival is gone before you arrive. The markets are disappointed in their statues.

choices.text: Tell them statues are only stone

effects.log: The merchants keep their statues anyway. Faith is like that.

events.text: The page of the Book of Fates with your name at the top has begun to fill, one line a century. A friendly clerk copies each line and sends it to you. This century's line: "The Star looked back."

choices.text: Ask for every line from now on

effects.log: The clerk agrees. Every century you get one line of yourself, as fate writes it.
They stop. You wonder about it every century.

events.text: This century's line in the Book of Fates: "The Star went quietly." You have not gone anywhere. You check the ledger. You did not raid anything, all century, and did not notice.

effects.log: The next line says the same. And the one after.
The next line says: "The Star remembered." You are not sure that was the better line.

events.text: The friendly clerk who copies the Book of Fates for you has retired. Their last copy is not of this century's line: it is the next one, which fate has not yet written, but which the clerk could see coming. They wrote it down anyway.

effects.log: You read it. You keep it in your sleeve for the next hundred years and then it is true.
You burn it. The next century, fate writes something else.

events.text: A courtier of the Will of Heaven, sent to measure your mood, reports back that the Star's face shows nothing at all: not anger, not kindness, not boredom. They recommend that envoys bring no gifts, since there is no telling if they please.

effects.log: The envoy reports a smile. Nobody in the Will believes it.
The envoys bring nothing, and you are spared their gifts.

events.text: A god of a domain you have never raided kneels on your stair in the rain and will not get up until you promise never to come. They have knelt for three days. Their worshippers below are lighting candles.

effects.log: They get up, soaked, and bow, and go. You keep it.

choices.text: Tell them to get up and go home

effects.log: They stay. On the fifth day, you promise anyway.

events.text: The spears of your host have begun to rust in the long peace between raids. The armourer asks whether to sharpen them or let them rest. Your host is listening for the answer.

effects.log: The host's spears gleam again. Heaven sees the gleam from far off.
The spears rust a little more. The host takes up gardening.

events.text: The children of the isles sing a skipping-song about you. It counts the domains you have taken, one per skip, and the child who trips must be the Star. Nobody wants to trip.

effects.log: A child trips. They are very brave about being the Star.

choices.text: Ask Ryu Gaon if the count is right

effects.log: It is three short. You are oddly pleased.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has sent you a gift for the first time: a new string for a bow, the kind the isles make, very fine. There is no note. Ryu Gaon says it means they want a fair fight, with nothing to blame.

effects.log: You restring your bow with it. {sov_hunter} hears, and is satisfied.
A string from your vault goes to the isles. It is the strangest exchange of the hunt.

events.text: The mortals below {sov_domain} keep a festival for its god every spring, and this year they have kept it for you, in your colours, with your sign. It is a very nervous festival. Nobody dances.

effects.log: The sun comes out. A few of them start to dance.
The festival ends early. They will keep it again next year.

events.text: You find, in the corner of your hall, a young god who has hidden there to watch how a Calamity Star spends an ordinary day. They are disappointed. You read, you eat, you write letters. They had hoped for more.

effects.log: They watch one raid, and go home, and never come back.

choices.text: Give them a letter to deliver

effects.log: They deliver your letter, and decide you are an ordinary god after all.

events.text: The clerks of the Heavenly Court have a tea-room, and on its wall a list of every warrant ever served on you, and next to each, the name of the clerk who drew the duty. Gil Haneul's name is on the list more than anyone's.

effects.log: The clerks drink it nervously, and then gratefully.

choices.text: Send them your own warrant, to add

effects.log: You write a warrant against yourself. The clerks pin it on the wall, laughing.

events.text: An old enemy, a god you threw down two thousand years ago, has come to your gate with a teapot. They do not want their domain back. They want someone to drink tea with who remembers what heaven was like back then.

effects.log: You drink and remember together all afternoon. Neither of you mentions the raid.
They go. Their teapot stays on your stair for a week, and then it is gone too.

events.text: The Righteous Immortals have built a memorial to the six waves sent against you, at the place they gathered for the first. It lists the names of the fallen. At the bottom, someone has scratched your name too.

effects.log: Your name stays scratched under theirs. Nobody removes it.
You stand at the memorial for a day. The Righteous Immortals who see you do not draw.

events.text: The prayers that reach you from below are all the same kind: please pass us by. A scholar of your sky has counted them for a year and found exactly one that asked for something else. It asked you to come.

effects.log: It was a small mortal below, fighting a cruel lord. You pass over the lord. Once.
The one prayer goes unanswered. It does not come again.

events.text: You dream of the first raid you ever made, and in the dream you do not give the word. You stand at the edge of your sky with your hand raised and do not lower it, and the dream goes on for years.

choices.text: Lower the hand, in the dream

effects.log: You wake. The ledger is still the ledger.

choices.text: Keep it raised until you wake

effects.log: You wake with your arm aching. You do not raid that year.

events.text: It is the feast of your host's founding. The captains have set a seat at the head of the table for every captain who ever fell in your service. There are more empty seats than full ones.

effects.log: You sit at the far end, among them. The host goes quiet and then goes on.

choices.text: Take the head of the table

effects.log: You take the head. The empty seats face you all night.

events.text: Your shadow passes over a feast of the Green Assembly by accident, on your way somewhere else. Every god at the feast freezes, with cups halfway to their mouths. You are already gone. They stay frozen for a long time.

effects.log: You land at the feast and apologise. Nobody has ever seen that. They are more frightened than before.
They go back to their feast an hour later. Nobody laughs again that night.

events.text: A spoil from your vault has gone missing: a small bell from a domain you raided long ago. It turns up a year later, back in its own domain, hung on the gate again. Nobody admits to anything.

effects.log: The bell rings in its own gate. Nobody in your host is punished.
A cook of your host took it. They were born in that domain. You let them keep their post.

events.text: A star falls from your sky one night, a small one, nobody's. It lands below in a mortal field and the mortals there make it a shrine. They pray at it to the god whose sky it fell from.

effects.log: You answer a child who prays for their sick goat. The goat lives. The shrine grows.

choices.text: Let it be just a stone

effects.log: It is just a stone below. The mortals pray at it anyway.

events.text: The four Elder Lineages have written you a single letter together, which they have not done for any god in an age. It says only that they are watching, and that they have been watching since before you were born, and that this is not a threat.

effects.log: Your answer is one line. The Lineages argue about it for a century.
You keep it. It is the most frightening letter you have ever had, for no reason you can name.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has hung a portrait of you in the hall of warrants, as it does for every god it has warranted more than a hundred times. You are the first in a thousand years to earn one. It is not flattering.

effects.log: The new portrait is accurate. The clerks prefer the old one.
It hangs there, unflattering, forever.

events.text: The domain you took from {sov_god} dreams at night. Its fields murmur and its rivers turn over in their beds. Ryu Gaon says a domain dreams of the god it had before. Yours dreams of {sov_god}, every night.

effects.log: It dreams. You sleep badly, and so does it, and you are, in a way, company.
{sov_god} walks their old domain for a night. It sleeps soundly after.

events.text: It is raining on {sov_isle}, the first rain since your raid. The immortals are standing in it with their faces up. Ryu Gaon says the isle's arrays have been mended at last, and the rain is the first thing they let through.

effects.log: You keep your clouds from their sky. The rain is theirs.

choices.text: Send your own rain after it

effects.log: Two rains fall on {sov_isle}. The immortals go indoors.

events.text: {sov_hunter} has died, of age, on {sov_isle}, with their bow beside them, unstrung. The isle has sent a messenger to tell you, which they did not have to do. "They wanted you to know it was not you," the messenger says.

effects.log: You send a jar of starlight. It is placed on their grave.
You stand at the back. The isle knows. Nobody turns around.

events.text: You have received a letter addressed to the Calamity Star from a mortal child below. It asks whether you are lonely. It is in very large letters, and the child has drawn a star with a face.

effects.log: You send a dream. The child wakes up knowing the answer, and tells nobody.
It goes on the wall by Oh Sanggil's maps. It is the only picture of you that smiles.

events.text: There is no war in heaven this century. The gods who fought the last one meet in the markets and bow to each other stiffly. Your host has nothing to feed on. Mak Dohyeon or their successor asks whether to start something.

effects.log: Heaven rests. It is the longest peace in memory, and you are in it.
The peace breaks. Heaven blames you, correctly.

events.text: Your hall has gone completely silent. Not a captain speaks, not a servant moves. It is only, you realise after an hour, that you have been sitting very still and frowning, and the whole sky is waiting for you to stop.

effects.log: The hall breathes. Somebody drops a cup. Everyone laughs, nervously.
They wait another hour. It is a very long hour.

events.text: The gods of the twelve domains, or those who hold them now, have met for the first time since the founding of heaven. They have agreed on one thing: once a century, one of them will meet the Calamity Star in a fair duel, until one side is tired of it.

effects.log: The first duel is set. Heaven buys seats for it, quietly.
The Twelve take your refusal as a victory and say so in every hall.

events.text: The first duel of the Twelve: the god who holds the Mountains, slow and enormous, who simply stands, and lets you strike, and does not fall. At dusk they have not moved. Neither have you, for an hour.

ok.log: At midnight the mountain-god takes one step back. They bow. Heaven calls it a victory, and so do they.

fail.log: They do not move. At dawn you bow first.

effects.log: You sit. They sit. It is declared a draw, the first in the history of duels.

events.text: The fifth century of duels. This one is against the god who holds the Dreams, who will not fight awake. The duel is held in a dream, and you wake not knowing who won. Neither does heaven.

effects.log: You claim it. The god of Dreams does not argue. They only smile in their sleep.
You concede. The god of Dreams wakes up very surprised.

events.text: The Twelve have met again, and decided that the duels are over. Not because anyone won: because they have begun to look forward to them. "It is unseemly," their spokesgod says, "to enjoy one's enemy so much."

choices.text: Tell them you enjoyed it too

effects.log: The Twelve go home, troubled. The next century they invite you to dinner instead.
They give you one more, against all twelve at once. It is a very long day.

events.text: Under all the domains of heaven lies the First Cloud, on which the first gods stood. It has slept since then. Your raids, three thousand years of them, have shaken it, and this morning it has turned over in its sleep. Every domain in heaven tilted a little.

effects.log: You go down through the domains to the First Cloud. It is very quiet down there, and very white.

choices.text: Steady your own domains and wait

effects.log: Your domains steady. The rest of heaven tilts for a year.

events.text: The First Cloud is not a god, and not a thing. When you put your hand on it, it remembers everything that has ever stood on it, all at once, and among those memories is you, small, giving the word on your first day.

effects.log: You show it the green book of the things you did not destroy. It goes very still, and sleeps.
It sees everything. It sleeps again, troubled, and heaven tilts back.

events.text: The First Cloud has not stirred again. But on the bottom of your oldest domain, where it rests on the First Cloud, your gardeners have found handprints in the white, small and very old. One of them is the same size as yours.

effects.log: It fits. You leave it there a long while.
You lay cloth over them. Nobody else will see them while you hold the domain.

events.text: Yeom Taeil or whoever keeps your stores now has drawn up, without being asked, a list of everything you own: domains, spoils, a host, a ledger, a garden of arguing plants. At the bottom: "To whom?"

effects.log: You give away a domain a century. Heaven is more frightened of this than of any raid.
The list sits on your table. It gets longer.

events.text: You have given away half of what you took. The gods who received the domains do not know how to thank a Calamity Star, and so they send you nothing, and hold their festivals for you in secret, and you hear of them anyway.

effects.log: You stand at the back of a festival held in your honour, unknown. It is a good festival.
You give away all of it except the ledger. Your sky is very bare.

events.text: Your sky is almost empty now. Your host has dwindled to the captains who would not leave. The gods of heaven still close their markets when your shadow passes. You have nothing left to take anything with. The fear goes on without you.

effects.log: You walk through a market. It closes. Then, stall by stall, it opens again behind you.

choices.text: Sit on your stair and watch heaven

effects.log: You sit. Heaven goes about its business, and keeps one eye on you.

events.text: Somebody in your host has counted the gods of heaven who have never met you, never been raided by you, never closed a market for you. There are eleven. They are all very young.

effects.log: They grow up in a heaven where the Star is a story.
You meet one. They are not afraid. They will be, they say, if you give them a reason.

events.text: A herald of the Throne of Storms has fainted in your hall in the middle of a message. Your captains are standing around them, not knowing what to do. The message was a complaint about the weather.

effects.log: They wake, see you, and faint again. The third time, they finish the message.
It is a long complaint about rain. You agree to some of it.

events.text: Your host's best cook was a captive from a raided domain, long ago, who stayed. They have asked to go home now, for the first time in four hundred years. Their domain's god is still alive, and has asked for them.

effects.log: They go home and cook for their old god. Your host eats badly for a century.

choices.text: Ask them to teach someone first

effects.log: They teach three apprentices and go. The food is almost as good.

events.text: A map of your sky drawn by the hunters of the isles has a mistake in it: a gate where there is no gate. Your host has found three hunters waiting at the place for a month, very patiently, for a gate that does not exist.

effects.log: You build one. The hunters walk through it, puzzled, and go home.
They take it home, red-faced. The next hunters come to the right gate.

events.text: {sov_god}, from whom you took {sov_domain}, has asked to visit it once, on its old feast day. They will come alone, unarmed, and leave at sunset. They have written it all out very carefully, as if afraid you will misunderstand.

effects.log: {sov_god} walks their old domain all day. At sunset they leave a flower on the gate.
{sov_god} spends the feast day at your border, looking in.

events.text: The Heavenly Court has declared a holiday on the day you were first warranted. It is not a celebration: clerks are given the day off to rest from you. They go on picnics.

effects.log: You raid nothing on the clerks' holiday, ever. They notice.

choices.text: Send a warrant of your own, as a joke

effects.log: The clerks come back from their picnics to find it. They frame it.

events.text: It is the anniversary of your raid on {sov_isle}. The isle keeps it as a day of silence: no bell, no voice, no fire. From your sky you can see it, a dark place in the bright cloud-sea.

effects.log: Your sky keeps it with them, every year. The isle notices, and does not say so.
You look away. The isle stays dark until dawn.

events.text: A relic of the waves has been brought to your gate by a trader: the broken knife of moonlight of one of the twins of the Silent Hall. They want a fortune for it. They found it in the cloud-sea.

choices.text: Buy it and send it to the Silent Hall

effects.log: The Hall receives it in silence. A grey pebble arrives on your stair.
They sell it to a collector of the Will of Heaven. It is displayed under glass.

events.text: A new god of the Green Assembly, very young, has asked their elders why the Calamity Star may never be seated in a pantheon. The elders have no answer but the old rule. The young god has written to you to ask instead.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: you never asked

effects.log: The young god reads it to the Assembly. It is debated for a century.

choices.text: Tell them a star needs no seat

effects.log: The young god writes back: everyone needs a seat. You keep the letter.

events.text: At the feast of your host, a captain raises a toast to the domains you have not yet taken. The hall cheers. In the corner, a captain who was born in a raided domain does not raise their cup.

choices.text: Raise yours to the one who did not

effects.log: You raise your cup to them. The hall goes quiet and then, slowly, raises its cups too.

choices.text: Raise your cup to the toast

effects.log: The hall drinks. The captain in the corner leaves early.

events.text: A comet has appeared in the sky of {sov_world}, your Pocket World, and its people say it is you, watching. It is not. It is only a comet. They have begun to hide indoors when it rises.

effects.log: The comet leaves. {sov_world} comes out of doors again.
It stays. {sov_world} learns to live with being watched, even by a comet.

events.text: A god you have never met bows to you in the street of a market of heaven, very low, and walks on. When you ask your captain who it was, they do not know. Later you learn they were grateful: you raided the god who had wronged them.

choices.text: Find them and refuse the thanks

effects.log: You find them. They insist. You let them, in the end.
Heaven is full of reasons. That was one.

events.text: An exile of the Heavenly Court has written to you from the far edge of heaven: "They say you are worse than me. I wanted to ask if it is true." It is signed with a name you do not know.

effects.log: They write back: thank you. It is the shortest correspondence in your ledger.

choices.text: Write back: nobody is worse than anyone

effects.log: They do not answer. You hear, later, that they went home to the Court.

events.text: You dream of your host marching without you, into a domain that does not exist, and coming back with nothing, and being happy. You wake and find your captains are already up, polishing nothing.

choices.text: Let them have a free day

effects.log: Your host spends a day at leisure. Some of them have never had one.
They drill. The dream fades.

events.text: The Lineage of the Root has sent its yearly note on your debt. It has not grown. It has not shrunk. At the bottom, in a different hand, someone has added: "We are in no hurry."

effects.log: You send a seed. The Root sends back a receipt for exactly one seed.
It goes in a drawer with the others. The drawer is full.

events.text: A child of {sov_god} who was not born when you took {sov_domain} has come to see the domain their parent lost. They do not hate you. They never knew it as theirs. They only want to know what it was like.

effects.log: You walk them through the domain and tell them what it was. They are quiet.
Their parent tells them. It takes all night. They never visit again.

events.text: You have not raided in a century. Nobody in heaven knows whether you will again. The not knowing has become a thing of its own: gods plan their festivals around it, and their wars, and their weddings.

effects.log: You raid a small domain. Heaven breathes out. At least it knows.
Heaven lives with not knowing. It turns out to be the most terrible thing you have done.

events.text: {sov_Isle}, the power you served in the Upper Realm before you were a god, has sent you a message: it is still teaching your first form to its young. It wanted you to know. It does not say why.

effects.log: You send the form that came after. The isle teaches it as yours.
They go on teaching the first. It is enough for them.

events.text: It is raining in the great market of the Will of Heaven, and every merchant has fled from the rain except one, who is under the same awning as you, both of you waiting for it to stop. They have not recognised you.

effects.log: You talk about the rain for an hour. It is the best hour you have had in a century.
They do not run. They nod and say, "Still raining."

events.text: A young god has come to your gate to tell you that they will be the next Calamity Star, after you. They are very serious and very sure, and they have brought a ledger of their own, empty.

choices.text: Tell them to write the first page well

effects.log: They go home and think about it for a century before writing anything.
They do not listen. They go anyway. You knew they would.

choices.text: Ask what they will write first

effects.log: They do not know. That is a good sign, you tell them.

events.text: A clerk of the Book of Fates has told you, in confidence, that the page with your name on it has a blank space at the bottom that the Book will not fill. It has never refused to fill a space before.

effects.log: The space stays blank. It is the only blank space in the Book.
You may not. The clerk is very firm. You respect them for it.

events.text: Someone has spilled tea on the ledger, across three centuries of raids. The ink has run. Whole domains are now a brown stain with a few letters showing. The captain responsible has confessed and is waiting by the door.

effects.log: Three centuries of your raids are a tea stain now. It is oddly restful to look at.

choices.text: Write them out again from memory

effects.log: You remember every one. That is the worst part.

events.text: A crowd of gods at a festival of the Heavenly Calendar parts in front of you like water before a prow. On the far side a very old god of the Silent Hall has not moved, because they did not hear you coming.

effects.log: You walk around the old god. The crowd watches you do it in silence.
They notice, at last, and smile, and step aside, slowly.

events.text: Mak Dohyeon's maps of the domains of heaven cover a whole wall of your war-room. Every domain you have taken is shaded grey. Today a captain points out that more than half the wall is grey now, and asks what happens when it is all grey.

effects.log: The captain nods. Nobody shades another domain that year.
You shade it. The captain does not ask again.

events.text: The heir of the tea-house at the gate of the raided isle still pours for any god who comes. When your captain passes through, the heir pours them a cup and asks after your health, as Seol Harin taught them.

effects.log: The heir writes back that the tea-house is well, and the gate is well, and so are the hunters.

choices.text: Go and drink a cup yourself

effects.log: You drink at the gate. The heir does not spill a drop.

events.text: Gil Haneul, the clerk of warrants, has had a child, and the child has made you a warrant of their own: a scrap of paper ordering the Calamity Star to come to tea. Gil Haneul sends it on, very apologetic.

effects.log: You come to tea at the clerk's house. The child is very stern about it.
You send a formal reply, sealed. The child keeps it all their life.

events.text: The domains you have taken each had a bell for their god's hours. They all hang in your hall now, and at dawn they ring together, a dozen gods' mornings at once, none of them in time with the others.

effects.log: They ring as one now. It is beautiful and wrong.

choices.text: Let them ring out of time

effects.log: They ring as they always did, each for its own lost god.

events.text: A white pebble has been left on your stair, as Baek Yuhwa used to leave them, long after the last of their letters. There is no letter under it. Only the pebble.

effects.log: It goes in the jar with the grey ones. The jar is nearly full.

choices.text: Leave one of your own in return

effects.log: You leave a black pebble at the edge of your sky. In the morning it is gone.

events.text: A captain of your host, a thousand years in service, has asked to retire to a domain you raided long ago, where they want to grow rice. The domain's new god has said they may come, if they leave their spear at the border.

effects.log: The captain leaves the spear at the border and goes in. They write that the rice is good.

choices.text: Give them a domain of your own instead

effects.log: They take it, and grow rice there too, a little sadly.

events.text: The Throne of Storms has sent an envoy who speaks only in weather. They stand in your hall and it rains on them, softly, and then the rain stops, and then a little thunder. Yun Hwaseol translates: it is an apology.

effects.log: You let the sun into your hall. The envoy dries and bows and goes.
It is for a hailstorm three centuries ago. You had forgotten it. They had not.

events.text: It is the anniversary of the day you gave the word, at the edge of your sky. Your host gathers there every year now, without orders, and waits to see if you will give it again.

effects.log: You give the word. The host goes out. Heaven remembers what it was afraid of.

choices.text: Raise your hand and hold it

effects.log: You hold it raised until dusk. The host goes home, and nobody is sure what they saw.
